sentences.zh: 自古后族，能以德禮進退、全宗保名者，鮮矣。

translations.literal: From ancient times among clans of empresses, those who could advance and withdraw through virtue and propriety and preserve their clan and reputation have been few.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, few among empresses' kin have managed to conduct themselves with virtue and propriety, stepping forward or back as circumstances required, and so preserve both clan and renown.

sentences.zh: 蓋恃宮掖之寵，接宴私之歡，高爵厚祿驕其內，聲色服玩惑於外；

translations.literal: For they rely on favor within the palace precincts and enjoy private banquets and pleasures; high ranks and generous stipends make them arrogant within, while music, beauty, clothing, and curios beguile them without.
translations.idiomatic: They rely on favor within the inner palace and the pleasures of private feasts; lofty titles and rich stipends feed their pride, while sensual delights, fine attire, and luxuries distract them without.

sentences.zh: 莫知師友之訓，不達危亡之道。

translations.literal: They know nothing of the instruction of teachers and friends, and do not grasp the path to danger and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: They heed neither the counsel of teachers nor friends, and never learn the road to ruin.

sentences.zh: 故以中才處之，罕不覆敗；

translations.literal: Therefore when placed in such positions with only middling talent, few escape overthrow and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Hence even those of moderate ability, once placed in such positions, rarely escape destruction.

sentences.zh: 亦由重植之木，自然顛披也。

translations.literal: This is also like a heavily laden tree, which naturally topples and splits.
translations.idiomatic: It is like a tree burdened with too heavy a crown — it must sooner or later topple.

sentences.zh: 明哲之君，知驕侈之易滿，榮寵之難保；

translations.literal: A clear-sighted sovereign knows that pride and extravagance easily reach their limit, and that glory and favor are hard to keep.
translations.idiomatic: A wise ruler knows that arrogance and excess soon run their course, and that honor and favor are hard to hold.

sentences.zh: 授任各當其才，祿位不過其量；

translations.literal: He assigns offices each according to merit, and salaries and ranks do not exceed what men deserve.
translations.idiomatic: He appoints each man to a post fitting his ability and never grants salary or rank beyond his measure.

sentences.zh: 告之以天命不易，誡之以大義滅親；

translations.literal: He informs them that the Mandate of Heaven does not change lightly, and warns them with the great principle that public duty may require cutting off kin.
translations.idiomatic: He teaches them that Heaven's mandate is not trifled with and warns them that the greater principle may require sacrificing even one's own kin.

sentences.zh: 使居無過之地，永享不貲之福，與國終始，不失其所以親也。

translations.literal: Thus they dwell in a place without fault, forever enjoy boundless good fortune, and remain kin to the state from first to last, never losing the reason for their closeness.
translations.idiomatic: So they stand blameless, enjoy lasting fortune beyond measure, and remain bound to the dynasty to the end without forfeiting the grounds of their intimacy with the throne.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「震來虩虩，恐致福也。

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: "When Thunder comes, fearful and fearful — through fear one may attain blessing."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: "When Thunder comes, fearful and fearful — through fear one may attain blessing."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「婦子嘻嘻，失家節也。

translations.literal: " It also says: "The wife and child laughing and laughing — this is the loss of household discipline."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "The wife and child laughing and laughing — this is the loss of household discipline."

sentences.zh: 」與其愛而失節，曷若懼而致福？

translations.literal: " Better to foster fear and attain blessing than to indulge with love and lose discipline?
translations.idiomatic: Better to foster fear and attain blessing than to indulge with love and lose discipline?

sentences.zh: 魏氏懲漢人之敗，著矯枉之法：幼主嗣位，母后不得臨朝；

translations.literal: The Wei, taking warning from the Han collapse, established corrective laws: when a young lord succeeded, the empress dowager might not preside over court.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei, taking warning from the Han collapse, established corrective laws: when a young sovereign succeeded, the empress dowager might not preside over court.

sentences.zh: 外氏無功，時主不得封爵。

translations.literal: Relatives on the maternal side without merit might not be enfeoffed by the reigning sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Maternal kin without merit might not be enfeoffed by the reigning sovereign.

sentences.zh: 雖曰刻薄，而卞、甄之族，竟無大過。

translations.literal: Though called harsh, the Bian and Zhen clans never in the end committed great offenses.
translations.idiomatic: Though the laws were called harsh, the Bian and Zhen clans never in the end committed great offenses.

sentences.zh: 皇唐受命，長孫、竇氏以勛賢任職，而武氏、韋氏以盈滿致覆。

translations.literal: When Tang received the Mandate, the Zhangsun and Dou clans served through merit and virtue, whereas the Wu and Wei clans were overthrown through fullness and excess.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang received the Mandate, the Zhangsun and Dou clans served through merit and virtue, whereas the Wu and Wei clans were ruined through excess and overreach.

sentences.zh: 夫廢興者，豈天命哉，蓋人事也！

translations.literal: As for rise and fall — is it the Mandate of Heaven? It is human affairs!
translations.idiomatic: As for rise and fall — is it the Mandate of Heaven? It is human affairs!

sentences.zh: 竇威、長孫無忌各自有傳，其餘載其得失，為《外戚傳》，以存鑒誡焉。

translations.literal: Dou Wei and Zhangsun Wuji each has his own biography; the rest are recorded here for their successes and failures, compiled as the "Biographies of Empress Consorts' Relatives," to preserve them as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wei and Zhangsun Wuji each has his own biography; the rest are recorded here for their successes and failures in these Biographies of Empress Consorts' Relatives, to preserve them as a warning.

sentences.zh: =獨孤懷恩=

translations.literal: = Dugu Huai'en =
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Huai'en

sentences.zh: 獨孤懷恩，元貞皇后弟之子也。

translations.literal: Dugu Huai'en was the son of the younger brother of Empress Yuan Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Huai'en was the son of Empress Yuan Zhen's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 父整，隋涿郡太守。

translations.literal: His father Zheng was governor of Zhuo commandery under Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zheng was governor of Zhuo commandery under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 懷恩幼時，以獻皇后之侄，養於宮中。

translations.literal: When Huai'en was young, as nephew of Empress Xian, he was raised in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth, as nephew of Empress Xian, Huai'en was raised in the palace.

sentences.zh: 後仕為鄠縣令。

translations.literal: Later he served as magistrate of E county.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as magistrate of E county.

sentences.zh: 高祖平京城，授長安令。

translations.literal: When Gaozu pacified the capital region, he was appointed magistrate of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu pacified the capital region, he was appointed magistrate of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 在職嚴明，甚得時譽。

translations.literal: In office he was strict and enlightened and won great repute at the time.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was strict and fair-minded and won great repute.

sentences.zh: 及高祖受禪，擢拜工部尚書。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, Huai'en was promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu received the abdication, Huai'en was promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 時虞州刺史韋義節擊堯君素於蒲州，而義節文吏怯懦，頻戰不利。

translations.literal: At that time Wei Yijie, prefect of Yuzhou, was attacking Yao Junsu at Pu province, but Yijie, a civil official and coward, repeatedly fought without success.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wei Yijie, prefect of Yuzhou, was attacking Yao Junsu at Pu province, but Yijie, a civil official and a coward, repeatedly fought without success.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣懷恩代總其眾。

translations.literal: Gaozu sent Huai'en to replace him and take overall command of the army.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent Huai'en to replace him and take overall command of the army.

sentences.zh: 懷恩督兵城下，為賊所拒，頻戰不利。

translations.literal: Huai'en led troops beneath the walls but was repulsed by the rebels; he repeatedly fought without success.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en led troops beneath the walls but was repulsed by the rebels and repeatedly fought without success.

sentences.zh: 高祖切讓之，因是怨望。

translations.literal: Gaozu sharply rebuked him, and he therefore harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sharply rebuked him, and he therefore harbored resentment.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘗戲之曰：「弟姑子悉為天子，次當舅子乎？

translations.literal: Gaozu once joked with him: "The sons of my sisters-in-law have all become emperors — is it next the turn of the son of my wife's brother?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu once joked with him: "The sons of my sisters-in-law have all become emperors — is it next the turn of the son of my wife's brother?"

sentences.zh: 」懷恩遂自以為符命，每扼腕曰：「我家豈女獨富貴耶？

translations.literal: " Huai'en then took this as a sign of destiny; he often clutched his wrist and said: "Is my house alone to be denied wealth and honor because it has a woman?"
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en then took this as a sign of destiny; he often clutched his wrist and said: "Is my house alone to be denied wealth and honor because it has a woman?"

sentences.zh: 」由是陰圖異計。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he secretly plotted treason.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he secretly plotted treason.

sentences.zh: 時虞鄉南山多群盜。

translations.literal: At that time there were many bandits in the southern mountains of Yuxiang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there were many bandits in the southern mountains of Yuxiang.

sentences.zh: 劉武周將宋金剛寇陷澮州，高祖悉發關中卒以隸太宗，屯於柏壁。

translations.literal: Liu Wuzhou's general Song Jingang invaded and captured Fen province; Gaozu mobilized all the troops of Guanzhong to place under Taizong, who encamped at Baiyu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wuzhou's general Song Jingang invaded and captured Fen province; Gaozu mobilized all the troops of Guanzhong under Taizong, who encamped at Baiyu.

sentences.zh: 懷恩遂與解縣令榮靜、前五原縣主簿元君寶謀引王行本兵及武周連和，與山賊劫永豐倉而斷柏壁糧道，割河東地以啗武周。

translations.literal: Huai'en then conspired with Rong Jing, magistrate of Jie county, and Yuan Junbao, former chief clerk of Wuyuan county, to bring the forces of Wang Xingben and Liu Wuzhou into alliance, join with the mountain bandits to raid the Yongfeng granary and cut Baiyu's supply line, and cede the lands east of the River to bribe Liu Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en then conspired with Rong Jing, magistrate of Jie county, and Yuan Junbao, former chief clerk of Wuyuan county, to bring Wang Xingben's troops and Liu Wuzhou into alliance, join with the mountain bandits to raid the Yongfeng granary and cut Baiyu's supply line, and cede the lands east of the River to bribe Liu Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 事臨發，會夏縣人呂崇茂殺縣令，據縣起兵，應武周。

translations.literal: When the plot was about to be launched, a man of Xia county, Lü Chongmao, killed the magistrate and seized the county to raise troops in support of Liu Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was about to be launched, Lü Chongmao of Xia county killed the magistrate, seized the county, and raised troops in support of Liu Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣懷恩與永安王孝基、陜州總管於筠、內史侍郎唐儉攻崇茂。

translations.literal: Gaozu sent Huai'en together with Prince Yong'an Xiaoji, Area Commander of Shan province Yu Jun, and Secretariat Vice-Director Tang Jian to attack Chongmao.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent Huai'en together with Prince Yong'an Xiaoji, Area Commander of Shan province Yu Jun, and Secretariat Vice-Director Tang Jian to attack Chongmao.

sentences.zh: 宋金剛潛兵來襲，諸將盡沒。

translations.literal: Song Jingang secretly led troops to raid them; all the generals were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jingang secretly led troops to raid them, and all the generals were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 君寶與開府劉讓亦同陷於賊中，遂泄懷恩之謀。

translations.literal: Junbao and Palace Director Liu Rang were likewise captured by the enemy and there revealed Huai'en's plot.
translations.idiomatic: Junbao and Palace Director Liu Rang were likewise captured by the enemy and there revealed Huai'en's plot.

sentences.zh: 既而懷恩逃歸，高祖復令率師攻蒲州。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Huai'en fled back; Gaozu again ordered him to lead troops to attack Pu province.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Huai'en fled back, and Gaozu again ordered him to lead troops to attack Pu province.

sentences.zh: 唐儉在賊中，說賊將尉遲敬德，請使讓還，連和罷兵，遂使發其事。

translations.literal: Tang Jian, who was among the enemy, persuaded the rebel general Yuchi Jingde to request Rang's return and a pact to cease fighting, and thereby had the affair exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jian, who was among the enemy, persuaded the rebel general Yuchi Jingde to request Liu Rang's return and a pact to cease fighting, and thereby had the affair exposed.

sentences.zh: 會堯君素為其下所殺，小帥王行本以蒲州降，懷恩勒兵入據其城。

translations.literal: When Yao Junsu was killed by his subordinates and junior commander Wang Xingben surrendered Pu province, Huai'en led troops in and seized the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Junsu was killed by his subordinates and junior commander Wang Xingben surrendered Pu province, Huai'en led troops in and seized the city.

sentences.zh: 高祖將濟河，已御舟矣，會讓至，乃使召懷恩，懷恩不知事已泄，輕舟來赴。

translations.literal: Gaozu was about to cross the river and had already boarded his boat when Liu Rang arrived; he therefore sent to summon Huai'en, who did not know the matter had been exposed and came lightly in a small boat.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was about to cross the river and had already boarded his boat when Liu Rang arrived; he therefore sent to summon Huai'en, who did not know the matter had been exposed and came lightly in a small boat.

sentences.zh: 及中流而執之，收其黨按驗，遂誅之，時年三十六，籍沒基家。

translations.literal: Midstream he was seized; his accomplices were arrested and examined, and he was executed. He was thirty-six. His family's property was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Midstream he was seized; his accomplices were arrested and examined, and he was executed. He was thirty-six. His family's property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: =竇德明　=

translations.literal: = Dou Deming =
translations.idiomatic: Dou Deming

sentences.zh: 竇德明，太穆順聖皇后兄之孫也。

translations.literal: Dou Deming was the grandson of the elder brother of Empress Taimu Shunsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Deming was the grandson of Empress Taimu Shunsheng's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 祖照，尚後魏文帝女義陽公主，封鉅鹿公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhao married Princess Yiyang, daughter of Emperor Wen of Later Wei, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhao married Princess Yiyang, daughter of Emperor Wen of Later Wei, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Julu.

sentences.zh: 父彥，襲父封，仕隋為西平郡守。

translations.literal: His father Yan inherited his father's title and served Sui as governor of Xiping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan inherited his father's title and served the Sui as governor of Xiping commandery.

sentences.zh: 德明少師事陳留王孝逸，頗涉文史。

translations.literal: Deming in youth studied under Wang Xiaoyi of Chenliu and gained considerable knowledge of literature and history.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Deming studied under Wang Xiaoyi of Chenliu and gained considerable knowledge of literature and history.

sentences.zh: 會漢王諒作亂，遣其將綦良攻黎州。

translations.literal: When Prince Han Liang rebelled, he sent his general Qi Liang to attack Li province.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Han Liang rebelled, he sent his general Qi Liang to attack Li province.

sentences.zh: 德明時年十八，募得五千人，倍道而進，號令嚴整，一戰破之。

translations.literal: Deming was then eighteen; he recruited five thousand men, advanced at double speed, kept his orders strict and orderly, and broke the enemy in a single battle.
translations.idiomatic: Deming was then eighteen; he recruited five thousand men, advanced at double speed, kept his orders strict and orderly, and broke the enemy in a single battle.

sentences.zh: 以功累拜齊王府屬，坐事免。

translations.literal: For his merit he was repeatedly promoted to an appointment on the staff of the Prince of Qi, but was dismissed on account of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was repeatedly promoted to an appointment on the staff of the Prince of Qi, but was dismissed on account of an offense.

sentences.zh: 及義師圍長安，永安王孝基、襄邑王神符、江夏王道宗及高祖之婿竇誕、趙慈景並繫獄，隋將衛文升、陰世師欲殺之。

translations.literal: When the righteous army besieged Chang'an, Prince Yong'an Xiaoji, Prince of Xiangyi Shenfu, Prince of Jiangxia Daozong, and Gaozu's sons-in-law Dou Dan and Zhao Cijing were all imprisoned; the Sui generals Wei Wensheng and Yin Shishi wished to kill them.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army besieged Chang'an, Prince Yong'an Xiaoji, Prince of Xiangyi Shenfu, Prince of Jiangxia Daozong, and Gaozu's sons-in-law Dou Dan and Zhao Cijing were all imprisoned; the Sui generals Wei Wensheng and Yin Shishi wished to kill them.

sentences.zh: 德明謂文升曰：「罪不在此輩，殺之無傷於彼，適足招怨。

translations.literal: Deming said to Wensheng: "The guilt is not with these men; killing them would not harm the enemy but would only invite resentment."
translations.idiomatic: Deming said to Wensheng: "The guilt is not with these men; killing them would not harm the enemy but would only invite resentment."

sentences.zh: 」文升乃止。

translations.literal: " Wensheng then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng then stopped.

sentences.zh: 及謁見高祖，竟不自言，時人稱其長者。

translations.literal: When he had an audience with Gaozu, he never spoke of it himself; people at the time praised him as a man of mature character.
translations.idiomatic: When he had an audience with Gaozu, he never spoke of it himself; people at the time praised him as a man of mature character.

sentences.zh: 武德初，拜考功郎中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Wude era he was appointed Director in the Bureau of Merit.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wude era he was appointed Director in the Bureau of Merit.

sentences.zh: 從太宗擊王世充，頻有戰功，封顯武男。

translations.literal: He followed Taizong in attacking Wang Shichong, repeatedly won merit in battle, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Xianwu.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Taizong in attacking Wang Shichong, repeatedly won merit in battle, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Xianwu.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，歷常、愛二州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhenguan era he served successively as prefect of Chang and Ai provinces.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhenguan era he served successively as prefect of Chang and Ai provinces.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he died.

sentences.zh: 弟德玄，高宗時為左相。

translations.literal: His younger brother Dexuan served as Left Chancellor under Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Dexuan served as Left Chancellor under Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 德玄子懷貞。

translations.literal: Dexuan's son was Huai Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Dexuan's son was Huai Zhen.

sentences.zh: 懷貞，少有名譽，時兄弟宗族，並以輿馬為事，懷貞獨折節自修，衣服儉素。

translations.literal: Huai Zhen in youth had a fine reputation; at the time his brothers and clansmen all devoted themselves to carriages and horses, but Huai Zhen alone restrained himself and cultivated virtue, dressing plainly and simply.
translations.idiomatic: Huai Zhen in youth had a fine reputation; at the time his brothers and clansmen all devoted themselves to carriages and horses, but Huai Zhen alone restrained himself and cultivated virtue, dressing plainly and simply.

sentences.zh: 聖歷中為清河令，治有能名。

translations.literal: During the Shenglu era he served as magistrate of Qinghe and was known for capable administration.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenglu era he served as magistrate of Qinghe and was known for capable administration.

sentences.zh: 俄歷越州都督、揚州大都督府長史，所在皆以清幹著稱。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he served successively as Area Commander of Yue province and Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou Grand Area Command, and everywhere was known for integrity and efficiency.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he served successively as Area Commander of Yue province and Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou Grand Area Command, and everywhere was known for integrity and efficiency.

sentences.zh: ，累遷御史大夫，兼檢校雍州長史。

translations.literal: , he was promoted repeatedly to Censor-in-Chief and concurrently Acting Governor of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted repeatedly to Censor-in-Chief and concurrently Acting Governor of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 時韋庶人及安樂公主等干預朝政。

translations.literal: At that time the Deposed Consort Wei and Princess Anle and others interfered in court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Deposed Consort Wei and Princess Anle and others interfered in court affairs.

sentences.zh: 懷貞每諂順委曲取容，改名從一，以避后父之諱，自是名稱日損。

translations.literal: Huai Zhen always fawned and yielded to win favor; he changed his name to Congyi to avoid the taboo on the empress's father's name, and from then on his reputation daily declined.
translations.idiomatic: Huai Zhen always fawned and yielded to win favor; he changed his name to Congyi to avoid the taboo on the empress's father's name, and from then on his reputation daily declined.

sentences.zh: 庶人微時乳母王氏，本蠻婢也，特封莒國夫人，嫁為懷貞妻。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Consort was still obscure, her wet nurse Lady Wang, originally a barbarian slave girl, was specially enfeoffed as Lady of Ju state and given in marriage to Huai Zhen as his wife.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Consort was still obscure, her wet nurse Lady Wang, originally a barbarian slave girl, was specially enfeoffed as Lady of Ju state and given in marriage to Huai Zhen as his wife.

sentences.zh: 俗謂乳母之婿為阿沄，懷貞每因謁見之次及進表疏，列在官位，必曰「皇后阿沄」，時人或以「國沄」呼之，初無慚色。

translations.literal: Common speech calls a wet nurse's son-in-law a "Ayun"; whenever Huai Zhen had an audience or submitted a memorial listing his official rank, he always wrote "the Empress's Ayun," and people at the time sometimes called him "State Ayun" — yet he showed no shame at first.
translations.idiomatic: Common speech calls a wet nurse's son-in-law an "Ayun"; whenever Huai Zhen had an audience or submitted a memorial listing his official rank, he always wrote "the Empress's Ayun," and people at the time sometimes called him "State Ayun" — yet at first he showed no shame.

sentences.zh: 宦官用權，懷貞尤所畏敬，每視事聽訟，見無須者，誤以接之。

translations.literal: Eunuchs wielded power, and Huai Zhen feared and honored them above all; whenever he held court and heard cases, if he saw a beardless man he would mistakenly treat him as a eunuch and defer to him.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs wielded power, and Huai Zhen feared and honored them above all; whenever he held court and heard cases, if he saw a beardless man he would mistakenly treat him as a eunuch and defer to him.

sentences.zh: 監察御史魏傳弓嘗以內常侍輔信義尤縱暴，將奏劾之。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Wei Chuanggong once intended to memorialize and impeach Palace Attendant Fu Xinyi, who was especially violent and overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Wei Chuanggong once intended to memorialize and impeach Palace Attendant Fu Xinyi, who was especially violent and overbearing.

sentences.zh: 懷貞曰：「輔常侍深為安樂公主所信任，權勢甚高，言成禍福，何得輒有彈糾？

translations.literal: Huai Zhen said: "Attendant Fu is deeply trusted by Princess Anle; his power is very great and his words bring fortune or disaster — how can you rashly impeach him?"
translations.idiomatic: Huai Zhen said: "Attendant Fu is deeply trusted by Princess Anle; his power is very great and his words bring fortune or disaster — how can you rashly impeach him?"

sentences.zh: 」傳弓曰：「今王綱漸壞，君子道消，正由此輩擅權耳！

translations.literal: " Chuanggong said: "Today the royal norms are gradually breaking down and the way of the gentleman is fading — it is precisely because men like these monopolize power!"
translations.idiomatic: Chuanggong said: "Today the royal norms are gradually breaking down and the way of the gentleman is fading — it is precisely because men like these monopolize power!"

sentences.zh: 若得今日殺之，明日受誅，無所恨。

translations.literal: If I can kill him today and be executed tomorrow, I shall have no regret.
translations.idiomatic: If I can kill him today and be executed tomorrow, I shall have no regret.

sentences.zh: 」懷貞無以答，但固止之。

translations.literal: " Huai Zhen had no reply but firmly restrained him.
translations.idiomatic: Huai Zhen had no reply but firmly restrained him.

sentences.zh: 韋庶人敗，左遷濠州司馬。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Consort Wei fell, he was demoted to Military Advisor of Hao prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Consort Wei fell, he was demoted to Military Advisor of Hao prefecture.

sentences.zh: 尋擢授益州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was promoted and appointed Chief Administrator of the Yizhou Grand Area Command.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was promoted and appointed Chief Administrator of the Yizhou Grand Area Command.

sentences.zh: 以附會太平公主，累拜侍中、兼御史大夫，代韋安石為尚書左僕射，監修國史，賜爵魏國公。

translations.literal: By currying favor with Princess Taiping he was repeatedly promoted to Palace Attendant and concurrently Censor-in-Chief, replaced Wei Anshi as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, supervised compilation of the national history, and was granted the title Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: By currying favor with Princess Taiping he was repeatedly promoted to Palace Attendant and concurrently Censor-in-Chief, replaced Wei Anshi as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, supervised compilation of the national history, and was granted the title Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 睿宗為金仙、玉真二公主創立兩觀，料功甚多，時議皆以為不可。

translations.literal: Ruizong founded two abbeys for the Princesses Jinxian and Yuzhen; the estimated labor was very great, and opinion at the time held it inadvisable.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong founded two abbeys for the Princesses Jinxian and Yuzhen; the estimated labor was very great, and opinion at the time held it inadvisable.

sentences.zh: 唯懷貞贊成其事，躬自監役。

translations.literal: Only Huai Zhen approved the project and personally supervised the labor.
translations.idiomatic: Only Huai Zhen approved the project and personally supervised the labor.

sentences.zh: 懷貞族弟詹事司直維鍌謂懷貞曰：「兄位極臺袞，當思獻可替否，以輔明主。

translations.literal: Huai Zhen's clansman and younger cousin Wei Jian, Direct Clerk in the Household of the Heir Apparent, said to Huai Zhen: "Brother, you have reached the highest offices of state; you ought to think of offering approval or rejection to assist the enlightened sovereign."
translations.idiomatic: Huai Zhen's clansman and younger cousin Wei Jian, Direct Clerk in the Household of the Heir Apparent, said to Huai Zhen: "Brother, you have reached the highest offices of state; you ought to think of offering approval or rejection to assist the enlightened sovereign."

sentences.zh: 奈何校量瓦木，廁跡工匠之間，欲令海內何所瞻仰也？

translations.literal: Why instead measure tiles and timber and mingle with the craftsmen — what is there in this for the realm to look up to?
translations.idiomatic: Why instead measure tiles and timber and mingle with the craftsmen — what is there in this for the realm to look up to?

sentences.zh: 」懷貞不能對，而監作如故。

translations.literal: " Huai Zhen could not reply but continued supervising construction as before.
translations.idiomatic: Huai Zhen could not reply but continued supervising construction as before.

sentences.zh: 時人為之語曰：「竇僕射前為韋氏國沄，後作公主邑丞。

translations.literal: People at the time made a saying about him: "Vice Director Dou was first the Wei clan's State Ayun, and afterward became the princess's district aide."
translations.idiomatic: People at the time made a saying about him: "Vice Director Dou was first the Wei clan's State Ayun, and afterward became the princess's district aide."

sentences.zh: 」言懷貞伏事公主，同於邑官也。

translations.literal: " This meant that Huai Zhen served the princess like a district official.
translations.idiomatic: This meant that Huai Zhen served the princess like a district official.

sentences.zh: ，太平公主逆謀事泄，懷貞懼罪，投水而死。

translations.literal: , when Princess Taiping's treasonous plot was exposed, Huai Zhen, fearing punishment, threw himself into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Princess Taiping's treasonous plot was exposed, Huai Zhen, fearing punishment, threw himself into the water and died.

sentences.zh: 追戮其屍，改姓毒氏。

translations.literal: His corpse was posthumously punished; his surname was changed to Du.
translations.idiomatic: His corpse was posthumously punished; his surname was changed to Du.

sentences.zh: 德明族弟孝諶。

translations.literal: Deming's clansman and younger cousin was Dou Xiaochen.
translations.idiomatic: Deming's clansman and younger cousin was Dou Xiaochen.

sentences.zh: 孝諶，刑部尚書誕之子，昭成順聖皇后父也。

translations.literal: Dou Xiaochen was the son of Minister of Justice Dan and father of Empress Zhaocheng Shunsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Xiaochen was the son of Minister of Justice Dan and father of Empress Zhaocheng Shunsheng.

sentences.zh: 則天時，歷太常少卿、潤州刺史。

translations.literal: During the reign of Empress Zetian he served successively as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and prefect of Run province.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Empress Zetian he served successively as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and prefect of Run province.

sentences.zh: ，后母龐氏被酷吏所陷，誣與后咒詛不道，孝諶左遷羅州司馬而卒。

translations.literal: , the empress's mother Lady Pang was framed by a cruel official, falsely accused of cursing the empress with impiety; Dou Xiaochen was demoted to Military Advisor of Luo prefecture and died.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's mother Lady Pang was framed by a cruel official, falsely accused of cursing the empress with impiety; Dou Xiaochen was demoted to Military Advisor of Luo prefecture and died.

sentences.zh: 子希瑊、希球、希瓘，並流嶺南。

translations.literal: His sons Xi Zhang, Xi Qiu, and Xi Guan were all exiled to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Xi Zhang, Xi Qiu, and Xi Guan were all exiled to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，隨例雪免。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shenlong era they were cleared by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong era they were cleared by precedent.

sentences.zh: 景雲年，追贈李諶太尉、邠國公，希瑊襲爵。

translations.literal: In the Jingyun era Dou Xiaochen was posthumously granted Grand Marshal and Duke of Bin; Xi Zhang inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingyun era Dou Xiaochen was posthumously granted Grand Marshal and Duke of Bin; Xi Zhang inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 玄宗即位，加贈孝諶太保，希瑊等以舅氏，甚見優寵。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong ascended the throne, Dou Xiaochen was further posthumously granted Grand Guardian; Xi Zhang and the others, as maternal uncles of the emperor, received great favor.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong ascended the throne, Dou Xiaochen was further posthumously granted Grand Guardian; Xi Zhang and the others, as maternal uncles of the emperor, received great favor.

sentences.zh: 希瑊累遷太子少傅、豳國公，尋卒。

translations.literal: Xi Zhang was promoted repeatedly to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Duke of Bin, and shortly afterward died.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zhang was promoted repeatedly to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Duke of Bin, and shortly afterward died.

sentences.zh: 希球官至太子賓客，封冀國公，卒。

translations.literal: Xi Qiu reached the office of Guest of the Heir Apparent, was enfeoffed as Duke of Ji, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Qiu reached the office of Guest of the Heir Apparent, was enfeoffed as Duke of Ji, and died.

sentences.zh: 及卒，謚曰靖。

translations.literal: Upon his death he was given the posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his death he was given the posthumous title Jing.

sentences.zh: 希瓘初賜爵畢國公，後改名。

translations.literal: Xi Guan was first granted the title Duke of Bi state, and later had his name changed.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Guan was first granted the title Duke of Bi state, and later had his name changed.

sentences.zh: 初為左散騎常侍，及希球卒，因授開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: At first he served as Left Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; when Xi Qiu died, he was accordingly appointed Grand Master of the Palace with the Standing of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served as Left Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; when Xi Qiu died, he was accordingly appointed Grand Master of the Palace with the Standing of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 玄宗以早失太后，尤重外家，兄弟三人皆國公，食實封。

translations.literal: Because Xuanzong had lost his mother early, he especially valued his maternal kin; all three brothers were made dukes and received actual fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xuanzong had lost his mother early, he especially valued his maternal kin; all three brothers were made dukes and received actual fiefs.

sentences.zh: 子鍔，又尚玄宗女永昌長公主，恩寵賜賚，實為厚矣。

translations.literal: His son E also married Xuanzong's daughter, Princess Yongchang the Elder; the favor and gifts bestowed were truly generous.
translations.idiomatic: His son E also married Xuanzong's daughter, Princess Yongchang the Elder; the favor and gifts bestowed were truly generous.

sentences.zh: 而兄弟皆貪鄙，過自封植，又甚之。

translations.literal: Yet the brothers were all greedy and base, going too far in enriching themselves — and in this they went even further.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the brothers were all greedy and base, going too far in enriching themselves — and in this they went even further.

sentences.zh: ，有竇勉潛交巫祝，勉犯法，坐信其詭說，被停官，放歸田園。

translations.literal: , Dou Mian secretly associated with shamans and diviners; Mian violated the law, and Xi Guan, for believing his deceptive talk, was stripped of office and sent back to his estate.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Mian secretly associated with shamans and diviners; Mian violated the law, and Xi Guan, for believing his deceptive talk, was stripped of office and sent back to his estate.

sentences.zh: 尋以尊老，又授開府儀同三司，依舊朝會。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, on account of his advanced age, he was again granted Grand Master of the Palace with the Standing of the Three Excellencies and continued to attend court as before.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, on account of his advanced age, he was again granted Grand Master of the Palace with the Standing of the Three Excellencies and continued to attend court as before.

sentences.zh: 十三載十二月卒，玄宗哭於行在，贈司徒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the thirteenth year he died; Xuanzong wept at the temporary palace and posthumously granted him Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the thirteenth year he died; Xuanzong wept at the temporary palace and posthumously granted him Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 財貨鉅萬。

translations.literal: His wealth amounted to tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: His wealth amounted to tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 從父弟維鍌，好學，以撰著為業。

translations.literal: His younger cousin of the same grandfather, Wei Jian, loved learning and made authorship his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: His younger cousin of the same grandfather, Wei Jian, loved learning and made authorship his occupation.

sentences.zh: 時宗族咸以外戚，崇飾輿馬，維鍌獨清儉自守。

translations.literal: At the time the whole clan, as maternal kin, gloried in carriages and horses, but Wei Jian alone maintained himself in plain frugality.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the whole clan, as maternal kin, gloried in carriages and horses, but Wei Jian alone maintained himself in plain frugality.

sentences.zh: 中書令張說、黃門侍郎盧藏用、給事中裴子餘皆與之親善。

translations.literal: Chief Minister of the Secretariat Zhang Yue, Vice Director of the Chancellery Lu Zangyong, and Supervising Secretary Pei Ziyu were all on close terms with him.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister of the Secretariat Zhang Yue, Vice Director of the Chancellery Lu Zangyong, and Supervising Secretary Pei Ziyu were all on close terms with him.

sentences.zh: 官至水部郎中卒。

translations.literal: He reached the office of Director in the Bureau of Waterways and died.
translations.idiomatic: He reached the office of Director in the Bureau of Waterways and died.

sentences.zh: 撰《吉凶禮要》二十卷，行於代。

translations.literal: He compiled twenty juan of Essentials of Auspicious and Inauspicious Rites, which circulated in his age.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled twenty juan of Essentials of Auspicious and Inauspicious Rites, which circulated in his age.

sentences.zh: =長孫敞=

translations.literal: = Zhangsun Chang =
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Chang

sentences.zh: 長孫敞，文德順聖皇后之叔父也。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Chang was the uncle of Empress Wende Shunsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Chang was the uncle of Empress Wende Shunsheng.

sentences.zh: 仕隋為左衛郎將。

translations.literal: He served Sui as Commandant of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Sui as Commandant of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 煬帝幸江都，留敞守京城禁苑。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang visited Jiangdu, he left Chang to guard the imperial park of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang visited Jiangdu, he left Chang to guard the imperial park of the capital.

sentences.zh: 及義旗入關，率子弟迎謁於新豐，從平京城，以功除將作少監。

translations.literal: When the righteous banner entered the Pass, he led his sons and younger kinsmen to welcome and pay respects at Xinfeng; he followed in pacifying the capital and for his merit was appointed Vice Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous banner entered the Pass, he led his sons and younger kinsmen to welcome and pay respects at Xinfeng; he followed in pacifying the capital and for his merit was appointed Vice Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.

sentences.zh: 出為杞州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as prefect of Qi province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Qi province.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，坐贓免。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhenguan era he was dismissed on account of corruption.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhenguan era he was dismissed on account of corruption.

sentences.zh: 太宗以后親，常令內給絹以供私費。

translations.literal: Because he was the empress's kin, Taizong regularly had silk supplied from within the palace for his private expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was the empress's kin, Taizong regularly had silk supplied from within the palace for his private expenses.

sentences.zh: 尋拜宗正少卿，致仕加金紫光祿大夫，累封平原郡公。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan; upon retirement he was given the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan; upon retirement he was given the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈幽州都督，謚曰良，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: He died; he was posthumously granted Area Commander of You province, given the posthumous title Liang, and buried with honor at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He died; he was posthumously granted Area Commander of You province, given the posthumous title Liang, and buried with honor at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 從父弟　操敞從父弟操，周大司徒、薛國公覽之子也。

translations.literal: Younger cousin of the same grandfather, Cao. Chang's younger cousin of the same grandfather, Cao, was the son of Zhou Grand Minister of Education, Duke of Xue Lan.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's younger cousin of the same grandfather, Cao, was the son of Zhou Grand Minister of Education, Duke of Xue Lan.

sentences.zh: 武德中，為陜東道行臺金部郎中，出為陜州刺史。

translations.literal: During the Wude era he served as Director in the Bureau of Revenue on the Eastern Shaanxi Circuit Executive, then was sent out as prefect of Shan province.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wude era he served as Director in the Bureau of Revenue on the Eastern Shaanxi Circuit Executive, then was sent out as prefect of Shan province.

sentences.zh: 自州東引水入城，以代井汲，百姓於今利之。

translations.literal: He led water from east of the prefectural seat into the city to replace well-drawn water; the people benefit from this to this day.
translations.idiomatic: He led water from east of the prefectural seat into the city to replace well-drawn water; the people benefit from this to this day.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，歷洺州刺史、益揚二州都督府長史，並有善政。

translations.literal: During the Zhenguan era he served successively as prefect of Ming province and Chief Administrator of the Grand Area Commands of Yi and Yang provinces, and everywhere had good administration.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan era he served successively as prefect of Ming province and Chief Administrator of the Grand Area Commands of Yi and Yang provinces, and everywhere had good administration.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，以子詮尚太宗女新城公主，拜岐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, because his son Quan married Taizong's daughter Princess Xincheng, he was appointed prefect of Qi province.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, because his son Quan married Taizong's daughter Princess Xincheng, he was appointed prefect of Qi province.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，加金紫光祿大夫，賜爵樂壽男。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yonghui era he was given the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and granted the title Baron of Leshou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yonghui era he was given the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and granted the title Baron of Leshou.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈吏部尚書、并州都督，謚曰安。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he died; he was posthumously granted Minister of the Civil Service and Area Commander of Bing province, and given the posthumous title An.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he died; he was posthumously granted Minister of the Civil Service and Area Commander of Bing province, and given the posthumous title An.

sentences.zh: 詮官至尚書奉御。

translations.literal: Quan reached the office of Palace Attendant of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: Quan reached the office of Palace Attendant of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 詮即侍中韓瑗妻弟也。

translations.literal: Quan was the younger brother-in-law of Palace Attendant Han Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Quan was the younger brother-in-law of Palace Attendant Han Yuan.

sentences.zh: 及瑗得罪，事連於詮，減死配流巂州。

translations.literal: When Yuan was punished, the affair implicated Quan; his death sentence was commuted and he was exiled to Xi prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan was punished, the affair implicated Quan; his death sentence was commuted and he was exiled to Xi prefecture.

sentences.zh: 詮至流所，縣令希旨杖殺之。

translations.literal: When Quan reached his place of exile, the magistrate, seeking to please his superiors, had him beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Quan reached his place of exile, the magistrate, seeking to please his superiors, had him beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 趙持滿詮之甥有趙持滿者，工書善射，力搏猛獸，捷及奔馬；

translations.literal: Zhao Chiman, Quan's nephew — there was a Zhao Chiman who was skilled at calligraphy and archery, could wrestle fierce beasts by strength, and was as swift as a running horse.
translations.idiomatic: Quan's nephew Zhao Chiman was skilled at calligraphy and archery, could wrestle fierce beasts by strength, and was as swift as a running horse.

sentences.zh: 而親仁愛眾，多所交結，京師無貴賤皆愛慕之。

translations.literal: Moreover he was affectionate and benevolent toward the multitude and had many connections; in the capital none, high or low, failed to admire him.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he was affectionate and benevolent toward the multitude and had many connections; in the capital none, high or low, failed to admire him.

sentences.zh: 初為涼州長史，嘗逐野馬，自後射之，無不洞於胸腋，邊人深伏之。

translations.literal: At first he served as Chief Administrator of Liang province; he once chased wild horses and shot them from behind — none failed to be pierced through chest or flank — and the frontier people deeply admired him.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served as Chief Administrator of Liang province; he once chased wild horses and shot them from behind — none failed to be pierced through chest or flank — and the frontier people deeply admired him.

sentences.zh: 許敬宗懼其作難，誣與詮及無忌同反。

translations.literal: Xu Jingzong feared he would raise trouble and falsely accused him of conspiring with Quan and Wuji to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingzong feared he would raise trouble and falsely accused him of conspiring with Quan and Wuji to rebel.

sentences.zh: 及拷訊，終無異詞，且曰：「身可殺，辭不可奪。

translations.literal: Under torture he never changed his words and said: "My person may be killed, but my testimony cannot be taken away."
translations.idiomatic: Under torture he never changed his words and said: "My person may be killed, but my testimony cannot be taken away."

sentences.zh: 」吏竟代為款以殺之。

translations.literal: " The officials finally forged a confession on his behalf and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The officials finally forged a confession on his behalf and killed him.

sentences.zh: =武承嗣=

translations.literal: = Wu Chengsi =
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chengsi

sentences.zh: 武承嗣，荊州都督士矱之孫，則天順聖皇后兄子也。

translations.literal: Wu Chengsi was the grandson of Area Commander of Jing province Shiyue and the son of Empress Zetian Shunsheng's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chengsi was the grandson of Area Commander of Jing province Shiyue and the nephew of Empress Zetian Shunsheng.

sentences.zh: 初，士矱娶相里氏，生元慶、元爽。

translations.literal: At first Shiyue married Lady Xiangli and had Yuanqing and Yuanshuang.
translations.idiomatic: At first Shiyue married Lady Xiangli and had Yuanqing and Yuanshuang.

sentences.zh: 又娶楊氏，生三女：長適越王府功曹賀蘭越石，次則天，次適郭氏。

translations.literal: He then married Lady Yang and had three daughters: the eldest married Helan Yueshi, Functionary of the Prince of Yue's household; the second was Zetian; the third married into the Guo clan.
translations.idiomatic: He then married Lady Yang and had three daughters: the eldest married Helan Yueshi, Functionary of the Prince of Yue's household; the second was Zetian; the third married into the Guo clan.

sentences.zh: 士矱卒後，兄子惟良、懷運及元爽等遇楊氏失禮。

translations.literal: After Shiyue died, his brother's sons Weiliang and Huaiyun and Yuanshuang and the others treated Lady Yang with disrespect.
translations.idiomatic: After Shiyue died, his brother's sons Weiliang and Huaiyun and Yuanshuang and the others treated Lady Yang with disrespect.

sentences.zh: 及則天立為皇后，追贈士矱為司徒、周忠孝王，封楊氏代國夫人。

translations.literal: When Zetian was established as empress, Shiyue was posthumously granted Minister of Education and the title Loyal and Filial King of Zhou; Lady Yang was enfeoffed as Lady of Dai state.
translations.idiomatic: When Zetian was established as empress, Shiyue was posthumously granted Minister of Education and the title Loyal and Filial King of Zhou; Lady Yang was enfeoffed as Lady of Dai state.

sentences.zh: 賀蘭越石早卒，封其妻為韓國夫人。

translations.literal: Helan Yueshi died early; his wife was enfeoffed as Lady of Han state.
translations.idiomatic: Helan Yueshi died early; his wife was enfeoffed as Lady of Han state.

sentences.zh: 尋又加贈士矱為太尉，楊氏改封為榮國夫人。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Shiyue was further posthumously granted Grand Marshal; Lady Yang's title was changed to Lady of Rong state.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Shiyue was further posthumously granted Grand Marshal; Lady Yang's title was changed to Lady of Rong state.

sentences.zh: 時元慶仕為宗正少卿，元爽為少府少監，惟良為衛尉少卿。

translations.literal: At the time Yuanqing served as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan, Yuanshuang as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Manufactories, and Weiliang as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yuanqing served as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan, Yuanshuang as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Manufactories, and Weiliang as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 榮國夫人恨其疇日薄己，諷皇后抗疏請出元慶等為外職，佯為退讓，其實惡之也。

translations.literal: Lady Rong resented their past slighting of her and prompted the empress to submit a memorial requesting that Yuanqing and the others be sent to outside posts, feigning modesty while in fact hating them.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Rong resented their past slighting of her and prompted the empress to submit a memorial requesting that Yuanqing and the others be sent to outside posts, feigning modesty while in fact hating them.

sentences.zh: 於是元慶為龍州刺史，元爽為濠州刺史，惟良為始州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yuanqing was made prefect of Long province, Yuanshuang prefect of Hao province, and Weiliang prefect of Shi province.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yuanqing was made prefect of Long province, Yuanshuang prefect of Hao province, and Weiliang prefect of Shi province.

sentences.zh: 元慶至州病卒，元爽自濠州又配流振州而死。

translations.literal: Yuanqing reached his prefecture and died of illness; Yuanshuang was again exiled from Hao province to Zhen province and died there.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing reached his prefecture and died of illness; Yuanshuang was again exiled from Hao province to Zhen province and died there.

sentences.zh: 乾封年，惟良與弟淄州刺史懷運，以嶽牧例集於泰山之下。

translations.literal: In the Qianfeng era Weiliang and his younger brother Huaiyun, prefect of Zi province, assembled at the foot of Mount Tai according to the custom for mountain-sacrificing prefects.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianfeng era Weiliang and his younger brother Huaiyun, prefect of Zi province, assembled at the foot of Mount Tai according to the custom for mountain-sacrificing prefects.

sentences.zh: 時韓國夫人女賀蘭氏在宮中，頗承恩寵。

translations.literal: At the time Lady Helan, daughter of Lady Han, was in the palace and enjoyed considerable favor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Lady Helan, daughter of Lady Han, was in the palace and enjoyed considerable favor.

sentences.zh: 則天意欲除之，諷高宗幸其母宅，因惟良等獻食，則天密令人以毒藥貯賀蘭氏食中，賀蘭氏食之，暴卒，歸罪於惟良、懷運，乃誅之。

translations.literal: Zetian wished to eliminate them; she prompted Gaozong to visit their mother's residence, and when Weiliang and the others presented food, Zetian secretly had someone place poison in Lady Helan's food; Lady Helan ate it and died suddenly, and the blame was placed on Weiliang and Huaiyun, who were then executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zetian wished to eliminate them; she prompted Gaozong to visit their mother's residence, and when Weiliang and the others presented food, Zetian secretly had someone place poison in Lady Helan's food; Lady Helan ate it and died suddenly, and the blame was placed on Weiliang and Huaiyun, who were then executed.

sentences.zh: 仍諷百僚抗表請改其姓為蝮氏，絕其屬籍。

translations.literal: She further prompted the hundred officials to submit memorials requesting that their surname be changed to Fu and their clan registers severed.
translations.idiomatic: She further prompted the hundred officials to submit memorials requesting that their surname be changed to Fu and their clan registers severed.

sentences.zh: 元爽等緣坐配流嶺外而死，乃以韓國夫人之子敏之為士矱嗣，改姓武氏，累拜左侍極、蘭臺太史，襲爵周國公。

translations.literal: Yuanshuang and the others, implicated by association, were exiled beyond the Ling range and died; then Minzhi, son of Lady Han, was made Shiyue's heir, his surname was changed to Wu, he was repeatedly promoted to Left Attending Grand Secretary and Grand Astrologer of the Orchid Terrace, and inherited the title Duke of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshuang and the others, implicated by association, were exiled beyond the Ling range and died; then Minzhi, son of Lady Han, was made Shiyue's heir, his surname was changed to Wu, he was repeatedly promoted to Left Attending Grand Secretary and Grand Astrologer of the Orchid Terrace, and inherited the title Duke of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 仍令鳩集學士李嗣真、吳兢之徒，於蘭臺刊正經史，並著撰傳記。

translations.literal: He was further ordered to gather scholars such as Li Sizhen and Wu Jing at the Orchid Terrace to revise the classics and histories and also compose biographical works.
translations.idiomatic: He was further ordered to gather scholars such as Li Sizhen and Wu Jing at the Orchid Terrace to revise the classics and histories and also compose biographical works.

sentences.zh: 敏之既年少色美，烝於榮國夫人，恃寵多愆犯，則天頗不悅之。

translations.literal: Minzhi was young and handsome and had illicit relations with Lady Rong; relying on favor he committed many offenses, and Zetian was quite displeased with him.
translations.idiomatic: Minzhi was young and handsome and had illicit relations with Lady Rong; relying on favor he committed many offenses, and Zetian was quite displeased with him.

sentences.zh: ，榮國夫人卒，則天出內大瑞錦，令敏之造佛像追福，敏之自隱用之。

translations.literal: , when Lady Rong died, Zetian brought out great auspicious brocade from within the palace and ordered Minzhi to make Buddhist images for merit on her behalf; Minzhi secretly kept it for himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Rong died, Zetian brought out great auspicious brocade from within the palace and ordered Minzhi to make Buddhist images for merit on her behalf; Minzhi secretly kept it for himself.

sentences.zh: 又司衛少卿楊思儉女有殊色，高宗及則天自選以為太子妃，成有定日矣，敏之又逼而淫焉。

translations.literal: Moreover the daughter of Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Guard Yang Sijian was of exceptional beauty; Gaozong and Zetian personally selected her as crown princess and a date had been set, yet Minzhi forced himself upon her and violated her.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the daughter of Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Guard Yang Sijian was of exceptional beauty; Gaozong and Zetian personally selected her as crown princess and a date had been set, yet Minzhi forced himself upon her and violated her.

sentences.zh: 及在榮國服內，私釋衰绖，著吉服，奏妓樂。

translations.literal: While in mourning for Lady Rong he privately cast off his hemp mourning garments, put on festive dress, and had singing girls perform.
translations.idiomatic: While in mourning for Lady Rong he privately cast off his hemp mourning garments, put on festive dress, and had singing girls perform.

sentences.zh: 時太平公主尚幼，往來榮國之家，宮人侍行，又嘗為敏之所逼。

translations.literal: At the time Princess Taiping was still young and visited Lady Rong's household; palace women accompanied her, and she too was once forced by Minzhi.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Princess Taiping was still young and visited Lady Rong's household; palace women accompanied her, and she too was once forced by Minzhi.

sentences.zh: 俄而奸汙事發，配流雷州，行至韶州，以馬韁自縊而死。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward his licentious crimes were exposed; he was exiled to Lei province, and en route at Shao province he hanged himself with a horse bridle.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward his licentious crimes were exposed; he was exiled to Lei province, and en route at Shao province he hanged himself with a horse bridle.

sentences.zh: 承嗣，元爽子也。

translations.literal: Chengsi was Yuanshuang's son.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi was Yuanshuang's son.

sentences.zh: 敏之死後，自嶺南召還，拜尚衣奉御，襲祖爵周國公。

translations.literal: After Minzhi's death he was recalled from Lingnan, appointed Palace Attendant of the Imperial Wardrobe, and inherited his grandfather's title Duke of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Minzhi's death he was recalled from Lingnan, appointed Palace Attendant of the Imperial Wardrobe, and inherited his grandfather's title Duke of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 俄遷秘書監。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was transferred to Director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，追尊士矱為忠孝太皇，置崇先府官屬，五代祖已下，皆為王。

translations.literal: When Zetian presided over court, Shiyue was posthumously honored as the Loyal and Filial Grand Emperor; the Chongxian Office and its staff were established, and from the fifth-generation ancestor downward all were made kings.
translations.idiomatic: When Zetian presided over court, Shiyue was posthumously honored as the Loyal and Filial Grand Emperor; the Chongxian Office and its staff were established, and from the fifth-generation ancestor downward all were made kings.

sentences.zh: 嗣聖元年，以承嗣為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Sisheng, Chengsi was made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Sisheng, Chengsi was made Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 尋除太常卿、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and given the status of Associate Chief Minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and given the status of Associate Chief Minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 垂拱中，轉春官尚書，依舊知政事。

translations.literal: During the Chuigong era he was transferred to Minister of the Spring Office and continued as before to manage state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chuigong era he was transferred to Minister of the Spring Office and continued as before to manage state affairs.

sentences.zh: ，代蘇良嗣為文昌左相、同鳳閣鸞臺三品，兼知內史事。

translations.literal: , he replaced Su Liangsi as Left Chancellor of Wenchang, Associate of the Third Rank of the Phoenix Pavilion and Orchid Terrace, and concurrently managed Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He replaced Su Liangsi as Left Chancellor of Wenchang, Associate of the Third Rank of the Phoenix Pavilion and Orchid Terrace, and concurrently managed Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: ，於東都創置武氏七廟，追尊周文王為始祖文皇帝，王子武為睿祖康皇帝，云武氏之先也。

translations.literal: , at the Eastern Capital he newly established the seven ancestral temples of the Wu clan, posthumously honoring King Wen of Zhou as Founding Ancestor Emperor Wen and Prince Wu as Sagacious Ancestor Emperor Kang, declaring them the forebears of the Wu clan.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Capital he newly established the seven ancestral temples of the Wu clan, posthumously honoring King Wen of Zhou as Founding Ancestor Emperor Wen and Prince Wu as Sagacious Ancestor Emperor Kang, declaring them the forebears of the Wu clan.

sentences.zh: 后五代祖贈太原靖王居常為嚴祖成皇帝，高祖贈趙肅恭王克己為肅祖章敬皇帝，曾祖贈魏康王儉為烈祖昭安皇帝，祖贈周安成王華為顯祖文穆皇帝，考忠孝太皇為太祖孝明高皇帝，妣皆隨帝號曰皇后。

translations.literal: The empress's fifth-generation ancestor, posthumously granted King Jing of Taiyuan Juchang, was honored as Stern Ancestor Emperor Cheng; great-great-grandfather, posthumously granted King Su Gong of Zhao Keji, as Solemn Ancestor Emperor Zhang Jing; great-grandfather, posthumously granted King Kang of Wei Jian, as Majestic Ancestor Emperor Zhao An; grandfather, posthumously granted King Ancheng of Zhou Hua, as Illustrious Ancestor Emperor Wen Mu; father the Loyal and Filial Grand Emperor as Grand Ancestor Emperor Xiao Ming Gao — their consorts all followed the imperial titles as empresses.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's fifth-generation ancestor, posthumously granted King Jing of Taiyuan Juchang, was honored as Stern Ancestor Emperor Cheng; great-great-grandfather, posthumously granted King Su Gong of Zhao Keji, as Solemn Ancestor Emperor Zhang Jing; great-grandfather, posthumously granted King Kang of Wei Jian, as Majestic Ancestor Emperor Zhao An; grandfather, posthumously granted King Ancheng of Zhou Hua, as Illustrious Ancestor Emperor Wen Mu; father the Loyal and Filial Grand Emperor as Grand Ancestor Emperor Xiao Ming Gao — their consorts all followed the imperial titles as empresses.

sentences.zh: 元慶為梁憲王，元爽為魏德王。

translations.literal: Yuanqing was made King Xian of Liang, Yuanshuang King De of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing was made King Xian of Liang, Yuanshuang King De of Wei.

sentences.zh: 又追封伯父及兄弟俱為王，諸姑姊為長公主。

translations.literal: Paternal uncles and brothers were all posthumously enfeoffed as kings, and aunts and elder sisters as elder princesses.
translations.idiomatic: Paternal uncles and brothers were all posthumously enfeoffed as kings, and aunts and elder sisters as elder princesses.

sentences.zh: 於是封承嗣為魏王，元慶子夏官尚書三思為梁王，后從父兄子納言攸寧為建昌王，太子通事舍人攸歸為九江王，司禮卿重規為高平王，左衛親府中郎將載德為潁川王，右衛將軍攸暨為千乘王，司農卿懿宗為河內王，左千牛中郎將嗣宗為臨川王，右衛勛二府中郎將攸宜為建安王，尚乘直長攸望為會稽王，太子通事舍人攸緒為安平王，攸止為恆安王。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chengsi was enfeoffed as King of Wei; Yuanqing's son, Minister of the Summer Office Sansi, as King of Liang; the empress's elder male cousin's son, Remonstrating Secretary Youning, as King of Jianchang; Crown Prince's Communication Attendant Yougui as King of Jiujiang; Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Chonggui as King of Gaoping; Commandant of the Left Guard Personal Guard Zhonglang Jiang Zaide as King of Yingchuan; General of the Right Guard Youji as King of Qiansheng; Director of the Court of Imperial Granaries Yizong as King of Henei; Commandant of the Left Thousand-Ox Zhonglang Jiang Sizong as King of Linchuan; Commandant of the Right Guard Merit Second Office Zhonglang Jiang Youyi as King of Jian'an; Direct Attendant of the Imperial Carriage Youwang as King of Kuaiji; Crown Prince's Communication Attendant Youxu as King of Ping'an; and Youzhi as King of Heng'an.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Chengsi was enfeoffed as King of Wei; Yuanqing's son, Minister of the Summer Office Sansi, as King of Liang; the empress's elder male cousin's son, Remonstrating Secretary Youning, as King of Jianchang; Crown Prince's Communication Attendant Yougui as King of Jiujiang; Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Chonggui as King of Gaoping; Commandant of the Left Guard Personal Guard Zhonglang Jiang Zaide as King of Yingchuan; General of the Right Guard Youji as King of Qiansheng; Director of the Court of Imperial Granaries Yizong as King of Henei; Commandant of the Left Thousand-Ox Zhonglang Jiang Sizong as King of Linchuan; Commandant of the Right Guard Merit Second Office Zhonglang Jiang Youyi as King of Jian'an; Direct Attendant of the Imperial Carriage Youwang as King of Kuaiji; Crown Prince's Communication Attendant Youxu as King of Ping'an; and Youzhi as King of Heng'an.

sentences.zh: 又封承嗣男延基為南陽王，延秀為淮陽王，三思男崇訓為高陽王，崇烈為新安王，后兄子贈陳王承業男延暉為嗣陳王，延祚為咸安王。

translations.literal: Chengsi's sons Yanji and Yanxiu were enfeoffed as King of Nanyang and King of Huaiyang; Sansi's sons Chongxun and Chonglie as King of Gaoyang and King of Xin'an; the empress's elder brother's posthumously granted son, King of Chen Chengye's son Yanhui as Heir King of Chen, and Yanzuo as King of Xian'an.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi's sons Yanji and Yanxiu were enfeoffed as King of Nanyang and King of Huaiyang; Sansi's sons Chongxun and Chonglie as King of Gaoyang and King of Xin'an; the empress's elder brother's posthumously granted son, King of Chen Chengye's son Yanhui as Heir King of Chen, and Yanzuo as King of Xian'an.

sentences.zh: 承嗣嘗諷則天革命，盡誅皇室諸王及公卿中不附己者，承嗣從父弟三思又盛贊其計，天下於今冤之。

translations.literal: Chengsi once urged Zetian to change the dynasty and execute all the imperial princes and high officials who did not support him; Chengsi's younger cousin of the same grandfather Sansi also strongly praised the plan — the realm still resents this.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi once urged Zetian to change the dynasty and execute all the imperial princes and high officials who did not support him; Chengsi's younger cousin of the same grandfather Sansi also strongly praised the plan — the realm still resents this.

sentences.zh: 俄又賜承嗣實封千戶，仍監修國史。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Chengsi was granted an actual fief of one thousand households and continued to supervise compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Chengsi was granted an actual fief of one thousand households and continued to supervise compilation of the national history.

sentences.zh: 承嗣自為次當為皇儲，令鳳閣舍人張嘉福諷諭百姓抗表陳請，則天竟不許。

translations.literal: Chengsi considered himself next in line to be crown prince and had Phoenix Pavilion Drafter Zhang Jiafu prompt the common people to submit memorials requesting it, but Zetian would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi considered himself next in line to be crown prince and had Phoenix Pavilion Drafter Zhang Jiafu prompt the common people to submit memorials requesting it, but Zetian would not consent.

sentences.zh: ，授特進。

translations.literal: , he was granted Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted Special Advancement.

sentences.zh: 尋拜太子太保，罷知政事。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and removed from managing state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was appointed Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and removed from managing state affairs.

sentences.zh: 承嗣以不得立為皇太子，怏怏而卒，贈太尉、并州牧，謚曰宣。

translations.literal: Because Chengsi was not established as crown prince, he died discontented; he was posthumously granted Grand Marshal and Governor of Bing province, with the posthumous title Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Because Chengsi was not established as crown prince, he died discontented; he was posthumously granted Grand Marshal and Governor of Bing province, with the posthumous title Xuan.

sentences.zh: 子延基襲爵，則天避其父名，封為繼魏王。

translations.literal: His son Yanji inherited the title; Zetian avoided his father's name and enfeoffed him as Heir King of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yanji inherited the title; Zetian avoided his father's name and enfeoffed him as Heir King of Wei.

sentences.zh: 尋與其妻永泰郡主及懿德太子等，話及張易之兄弟出入宮中，恐有不利，後忿爭不協，泄之，則天聞而大怒，咸令自殺。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he, his wife the Princess of Yongtai commandery, Crown Prince Yide, and others discussed the Zhang Yizhi brothers' coming and going within the palace and feared harm; afterward, in angry disagreement, the matter was leaked; Zetian heard and was greatly enraged and ordered them all to kill themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he, his wife the Princess of Yongtai commandery, Crown Prince Yide, and others discussed the Zhang Yizhi brothers' coming and going within the palace and feared harm; afterward, in angry disagreement, the matter was leaked; Zetian heard and was greatly enraged and ordered them all to kill themselves.

sentences.zh: 復以承嗣次子延義為繼魏王。

translations.literal: Chengsi's second son Yanyi was again made Heir King of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi's second son Yanyi was again made Heir King of Wei.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，侍中敬暉等以唐室中興，武氏諸王宜削其王爵，乃率群官上表曰：

translations.literal: When Zhongzong ascended the throne, Palace Attendant Jing Hui and others, holding that the Tang house had been restored, argued that the Wu princes should be stripped of their royal titles; they therefore led the officials in submitting a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong ascended the throne, Palace Attendant Jing Hui and others, holding that the Tang house had been restored, argued that the Wu princes should be stripped of their royal titles; they therefore led the officials in submitting a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 中書舍人岑義之詞也。

translations.literal: This was the wording of Secretariat Drafter Cen Yi.
translations.idiomatic: This was the wording of Secretariat Drafter Cen Yi.

sentences.zh: 上答曰：

translations.literal: The emperor replied:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied:

sentences.zh: 於是降封梁王三思為德靜郡王，量減實封二百戶，定王、駙馬都尉攸暨為樂壽郡王，河內郡王懿宗為耿國公，建昌郡王攸寧為江國公，會稽郡王攸望為鄴國公，臨川郡王嗣宗為管國公，建安郡王攸宜為息國公，高平郡王重規為鄶國公，繼魏王延義為魏國公，安平郡王攸緒為巢國公，高陽郡王、駙馬都尉崇訓為酆國公，淮陽郡王延秀為桓國公，咸安郡王延祚為咸安郡公。

translations.literal: Thereupon King of Liang Sansi was demoted to Prince of Dejing commandery with a reduction of two hundred households from his actual fief; King Ding, Commandant of the Horse Guards Youji, to Prince of Leshou commandery; Prince of Henei commandery Yizong to Duke of Geng state; Prince of Jianchang commandery Youning to Duke of Jiang state; Prince of Kuaiji commandery Youwang to Duke of Ye state; Prince of Linchuan commandery Sizong to Duke of Guan state; Prince of Jian'an commandery Youyi to Duke of Xi state; Prince of Gaoping commandery Chonggui to Duke of Kuai state; Heir King of Wei Yanyi to Duke of Wei state; Prince of Ping'an commandery Youxu to Duke of Chao state; Prince of Gaoyang commandery, Commandant of the Horse Guards Chongxun to Duke of Feng state; Prince of Huaiyang commandery Yanxiu to Duke of Huan state; and Prince of Xian'an commandery Yanzuo to Duke of Xian'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon King of Liang Sansi was demoted to Prince of Dejing commandery with a reduction of two hundred households from his actual fief; King Ding, Commandant of the Horse Guards Youji, to Prince of Leshou commandery; Prince of Henei commandery Yizong to Duke of Geng state; Prince of Jianchang commandery Youning to Duke of Jiang state; Prince of Kuaiji commandery Youwang to Duke of Ye state; Prince of Linchuan commandery Sizong to Duke of Guan state; Prince of Jian'an commandery Youyi to Duke of Xi state; Prince of Gaoping commandery Chonggui to Duke of Kuai state; Heir King of Wei Yanyi to Duke of Wei state; Prince of Ping'an commandery Youxu to Duke of Chao state; Prince of Gaoyang commandery, Commandant of the Horse Guards Chongxun to Duke of Feng state; Prince of Huaiyang commandery Yanxiu to Duke of Huan state; and Prince of Xian'an commandery Yanzuo to Duke of Xian'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 中宗時，嗣宗至曹州刺史，攸宜工部尚書，重規岐州刺史，相次病卒。

translations.literal: During Zhongzong's reign Sizong reached prefect of Cao province, Youyi Minister of Works, and Chonggui prefect of Qi province; they died of illness one after another.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhongzong's reign Sizong reached prefect of Cao province, Youyi Minister of Works, and Chonggui prefect of Qi province; they died of illness one after another.

sentences.zh: 攸望至太常卿，左遷春州司馬而死。

translations.literal: Youwang reached Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was demoted to Military Advisor of Chun prefecture, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Youwang reached Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was demoted to Military Advisor of Chun prefecture, and died.

sentences.zh: 延秀伏誅後，武氏宗屬緣坐誅死及配流，殆將盡矣。

translations.literal: After Yanxiu was executed, Wu clansmen implicated by association were executed or exiled until nearly all were gone.
translations.idiomatic: After Yanxiu was executed, Wu clansmen implicated by association were executed or exiled until nearly all were gone.

sentences.zh: ，制削士彟帝號，依舊追贈太原王，妻楊氏亦削后號，依舊為太原王妃。

translations.literal: , an edict stripped Shiyue of his imperial title and restored the posthumous grant of King of Taiyuan; his wife Lady Yang likewise lost her empress title and was restored as Princess of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped Shiyue of his imperial title and restored the posthumous grant of King of Taiyuan; his wife Lady Yang likewise lost her empress title and was restored as Princess of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 承嗣子　延秀延秀，承嗣第二子也。

translations.literal: Chengsi's son Yanxiu. Yanxiu was Chengsi's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi's son Yanxiu was Chengsi's second son.

sentences.zh: 則天時，突厥默啜上言有女請和親，制延秀與閻知微俱往突厥，將親迎默啜女為妻。

translations.literal: During Zetian's reign the Türk Mo-ch'o reported that he had a daughter and requested a marriage alliance; Yanxiu was ordered to go with Yan Zhiwei to the Türks to personally welcome Mo-ch'o's daughter as his wife.
translations.idiomatic: During Zetian's reign the Türk Mo-ch'o reported that he had a daughter and requested a marriage alliance; Yanxiu was ordered to go with Yan Zhiwei to the Türks to personally welcome Mo-ch'o's daughter as his wife.

sentences.zh: 既而默啜執知微，入冠趙、定等州，故延秀久不得還。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Mo-ch'o seized Zhiwei and invaded Zhao, Ding, and other prefectures, so Yanxiu was long unable to return.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Mo-ch'o seized Zhiwei and invaded Zhao, Ding, and other prefectures, so Yanxiu was long unable to return.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，默啜更請通和，先令延秀送款，始得歸，封桓國公，又授左衛中郎將。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shenlong era Mo-ch'o again requested peace; he first had Yanxiu send pledges of submission, and only then was Yanxiu able to return; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Huan state and further appointed Commandant of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong era Mo-ch'o again requested peace; he first had Yanxiu send pledges of submission, and only then was Yanxiu able to return; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Huan state and further appointed Commandant of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 時武崇訓為安樂公主婿，即延秀從父兄，數引至主第。

translations.literal: At that time Wu Chongxun was Princess Anle's son-in-law — he was Yanxiu's older male cousin of the same grandfather — and repeatedly brought him to the princess's residence.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wu Chongxun, Princess Anle's husband and Yanxiu's older male cousin on their shared grandfather's side, repeatedly brought Yanxiu to the princess's residence.

sentences.zh: 延秀久在蕃中，解突厥語，常於主第，延秀唱突厥歌，作胡旋舞，有姿媚，主甚喜之。

translations.literal: Yanxiu had long been among the foreign lands and understood Türk language; often at the princess's residence Yanxiu would sing Türk songs and perform the Hu-xuan dance — he had graceful charm, and the princess greatly delighted in him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxiu had spent many years among the barbarians and knew Türk; at the princess's residence he often sang Türk songs and danced the whirling Hu-xuan dance. Graceful and alluring, he pleased the princess greatly.

sentences.zh: 及崇訓死，延秀得幸，遂尚公主。

translations.literal: When Chongxun died, Yanxiu gained favor and thereupon married the princess.
translations.idiomatic: After Chongxun died, Yanxiu won her favor and married the princess.

sentences.zh: 主，韋后所生男女中最小。

translations.literal: The princess was the youngest among the sons and daughters born to Empress Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was the youngest of the sons and daughters Empress Wei had borne.

sentences.zh: 初，中宗遷於房州，欲達州境，生於路次。

translations.literal: Initially, when Zhongzong was removed to Fang prefecture and had not yet reached the prefectural border, she was born along the way.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong was first sent into exile at Fangzhou and had not yet reached the prefecture, she was born on the road.

sentences.zh: 性惠敏，容質秀絕。

translations.literal: By nature she was intelligent and quick-witted; her appearance was surpassingly beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted by nature, she was also of surpassing beauty.

sentences.zh: 中宗、韋后愛龐日深，恣其所欲，奏請無不允許。

translations.literal: Zhongzong and Empress Wei doted on her more deeply day by day, indulging all her desires; no petition she submitted went ungranted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong and Empress Wei grew more indulgent toward her every day, granting her every wish without exception.

sentences.zh: 恃寵橫縱，權傾天下，自王侯宰相已下，除拜多出其門。

translations.literal: Relying on favor she acted with arrogant license; her power tilted the realm — from kings, marquises, and chancellors downward, most appointments and dismissals issued from her gate.
translations.idiomatic: Secure in imperial favor, she acted with arrogant impunity; her power overshadowed the realm, and from kings and chancellors down, most appointments came through her household.

sentences.zh: 所營第宅並造安樂佛寺，擬於宮掖，巧妙過之。

translations.literal: The residences she built and the Anle Buddhist Temple she erected were modeled on the imperial palace precincts, yet surpassed them in refinement.
translations.idiomatic: The mansions she built and the Anle Buddhist Temple she founded were modeled on the palace itself—and surpassed it in elegance.

sentences.zh: 令楊務廉於城西造定昆池於其莊，延袤數里。

translations.literal: She had Yang Wulian build Dingkun Pool west of the city at her estate, stretching several li.
translations.idiomatic: She had Yang Wulian construct the Dingkun Pool at her estate west of the city, a body of water several li across.

sentences.zh: 出降之時，以皇后仗發於宮中，中宗與韋后御安福門觀之，燈燭供擬，徹明如晝。

translations.literal: When she went out to marry, the empress's honor guard set out from within the palace; Zhongzong and Empress Wei mounted Anfu Gate to watch — lamps and candles were arranged in such profusion that night was bright as day.
translations.idiomatic: When she went forth to marry, the empress's honor guard departed from within the palace; Zhongzong and Empress Wei took their places at Anfu Gate to watch. Lamps and candles were set out in such abundance that the night shone bright as day.

sentences.zh: 延秀拜度日，授太常卿，兼右衛將軍、駙馬都尉，改封恆國公，實封五百戶。

translations.literal: Several days after Yanxiu performed the obeisance rites, he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, concurrently General of the Right Guard and Commandant of the Horse Guards; his fief was changed to Duke of Heng state with an actual fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: A few days after Yanxiu completed the marriage obeisances, he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, concurrently General of the Right Guard and Commandant of the Horse Guards; his title was changed to Duke of Heng with an actual fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 廢休祥宅，於金城坊造宅，窮極壯麗，帑藏為之空竭。

translations.literal: They demolished the Xiuxiang residence and built a mansion in Jincheng Ward, extravagantly magnificent to the utmost — the treasury was emptied on its account.
translations.idiomatic: They tore down the Xiuxiang residence and built a new mansion in Jincheng Ward, lavish beyond measure, draining the treasury dry.

sentences.zh: 崇訓子數歲，因加金紫光祿大夫、太常卿同正員、左衛將軍，封鎬國公，賜實封五百戶，以嗣其父。

translations.literal: Chongxun's son, still only a few years old, was accordingly given the titles Supervising Imperial Secretary with the Golden-purple Floppy and Minister of Ceremonies with Concurrent Regular Rank, and General of the Left Guard; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Hao state with a grant of five hundred actual fief households to succeed his father.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxun's son, only a few years old, was made Supervising Imperial Secretary with the Golden-purple Floppy, Regular-ranked Minister of Ceremonies, and General of the Left Guard; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Hao with five hundred actual fief households to succeed his father.

sentences.zh: 公主產男滿月，中宗、韋后幸其第，就第放赦，遣宰臣李嶠、文士宋之問、沈佺期、張說、閻朝隱等數百人賦詩美之。

translations.literal: When the princess's baby boy reached one month, Zhongzong and Empress Wei visited her residence, proclaiming an amnesty right there; they sent several hundred ministers and literary men — Chancellor Li Qiao, Song Zhiwen, Shen Quanqi, Zhang Yue, Yan Chaoyin, and others — to compose poems in praise.
translations.idiomatic: When the princess's newborn son completed his first month, Zhongzong and Empress Wei visited her residence and proclaimed an amnesty on the spot. They dispatched several hundred court ministers and literati—including Li Qiao, Song Zhiwen, Shen Quanqi, Zhang Yue, and Yan Chaoyin—to compose poems in celebration.

sentences.zh: 延秀既恃恩，放縱無所忌憚。

translations.literal: Yanxiu, now relying on imperial favor, acted with unchecked license and feared nothing.
