translations.idiomatic: Yanxiu, emboldened by imperial favor, gave himself over to reckless excess without restraint.

sentences.zh: 又公主府倉曹符鳳知延秀有不臣之心，遂說曰：「今天下蒼生，猶以武氏為念，大周必可再興。

translations.literal: Moreover Fufeng, warehouse clerk of the princess's household, knew Yanxiu harbored disloyal ambitions and therefore urged him, saying: "Today the people of the realm still hold the Wu clan in mind — the Great Zhou can surely rise again.
translations.idiomatic: The princess's household warehouse clerk Fufeng, perceiving Yanxiu's disloyal ambitions, urged him: "The people of the realm still look to the House of Wu—the Great Zhou can surely rise again.

sentences.zh: 按讖書云『黑衣神孫披天裳』，駙馬即神皇之孫也。

translations.literal: According to prophecy books it says, 'The divine grandson in black robes spreads heaven's garment' — the imperial son-in-law is precisely the divine empress's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Prophecy books say, 'The divine grandson in black robes spreads heaven's garment'—and you, the imperial son-in-law, are the divine empress's grandson.

sentences.zh: 」每勸令著皁襖子以應之。

translations.literal: " He constantly urged him to wear black jackets to correspond to the prophecy.
translations.idiomatic: " He repeatedly urged Yanxiu to wear black jackets to fulfill the prophecy.

sentences.zh: 及韋庶人敗，延秀與公主在內宅，格戰良久。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Consort Wei fell, Yanxiu and the princess were in the inner quarters and fought at close quarters for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Consort Wei fell, Yanxiu and the princess barricaded themselves in the inner quarters and fought hand to hand for a long while.

sentences.zh: 皆斬之。

translations.literal: Both were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Both were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 後追貶為悖逆庶人。

translations.literal: Later she was posthumously demoted to Commoner of Rebellion and Treason.
translations.idiomatic: She was later posthumously stripped of rank and demoted to Commoner of Rebellion and Treason.

sentences.zh: 元慶子　三思三思，元慶子也。

translations.literal: Yuanqing's son Sansi. Sansi was Yuanqing's son.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing's son Sansi was Yuanqing's son.

sentences.zh: 少以后族累轉右衛將軍。

translations.literal: In youth, through his connection to the empress's clan he was repeatedly transferred until he became General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he rose through the empress's kinship network, eventually becoming General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，擢拜夏官尚書。

translations.literal: When Zetian held court, he was promoted and appointed Minister of the Summer Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Zetian assumed the regency, he was promoted to Minister of the Summer Office.

sentences.zh: 及革命，封梁王，賜實封一千戶。

translations.literal: At the dynasty's transformation he was enfeoffed as King of Liang and granted an actual fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When she declared the new dynasty, he was enfeoffed as King of Liang with an actual fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 尋拜天官尚書。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed Minister of the Personnel Office.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was appointed Minister of the Personnel Office.

sentences.zh: ，轉春官尚書，監修國史。

translations.literal: , was transferred to Minister of the Office of Rites and placed in charge of compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of the Office of Rites and placed in charge of compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: ，檢校內史。

translations.literal: , and made Acting Imperial Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made Acting Imperial Secretary.

sentences.zh: 二年，進拜特進、太子賓客，仍並依舊監修國史。

translations.literal: In the second year he was promoted to Special Advancement and Companion to the Heir Apparent, while still continuing in charge of compiling the national history as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was promoted to Special Advancement and Companion to the Heir Apparent, while continuing to oversee compilation of the national history as before.

sentences.zh: 三思略涉文史，性傾巧便僻，善事人，由是特蒙信任。

translations.literal: Sansi had some acquaintance with letters and history; by nature he was inclined toward craftiness and crooked ease, skilled at pleasing people — hence he received special trust.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi had some literary and historical learning; crafty and ingratiating by nature, he excelled at winning people over and thereby earned Zetian's special trust.

sentences.zh: 則天數幸其第，賞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: Zetian often visited his residence, bestowing rewards of great richness.
translations.idiomatic: Zetian often visited his home, lavishing rich rewards upon him.

sentences.zh: 時薛懷義、張易之、昌宗皆承恩顧。

translations.literal: At the time Xue Huaiyi, Zhang Yizhi, and Changzong all received imperial favor and attention.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xue Huaiyi, Zhang Yizhi, and Changzong all enjoyed the empress's favor.

sentences.zh: 三思與承嗣每折節事之。

translations.literal: Sansi and Chengsi would each humble themselves to serve them.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi and Chengsi humiliated themselves in serving them.

sentences.zh: 懷義欲乘馬，承嗣、三思必為之執轡。

translations.literal: When Huaiyi wished to mount a horse, Chengsi and Sansi would invariably hold the reins for him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Huaiyi wanted to mount a horse, Chengsi and Sansi would hold the reins for him.

sentences.zh: 又贈昌宗詩，盛稱昌宗才貌是王子晉後身，仍令朝士遞相屬和。

translations.literal: He also presented Changzong with a poem lavishly praising Changzong's talent and appearance as the reincarnation of Prince Zijin, and had court officials compose responding verses in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Changzong a poem extravagantly praising his talent and looks as the reincarnation of Prince Zijin, and had court officials compose matching verses in turn.

sentences.zh: 三思又以則天厭居深宮，又欲與張易之、昌宗等扈從馳騁，以弄其權。

translations.literal: Sansi also, because Zetian was weary of dwelling deep within the palace, wished to accompany Zhang Yizhi, Changzong, and the others in riding and hunting at full gallop, thereby to wield his power for sport.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi also knew that Zetian was weary of the deep palace; he wanted to ride and hunt at her side with Zhang Yizhi, Changzong, and the rest, thereby to play with power in the open.

sentences.zh: 乃請創造三陽宮於嵩高山，興泰宮於萬壽山，請則天每歲臨幸，前後工役甚眾，百姓怨之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he requested the creation of Sanyang Palace on Mount Song and Xingtai Palace on Mount Wanshou, asking that Zetian visit each year — laborers were exceedingly numerous before and after, and the common people resented it.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore petitioned to build Sanyang Palace on Mount Song and Xingtai Palace on Mount Wanshou, asking that Zetian visit each year. The labor levies were enormous, and the people groaned under them.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，進拜司空、同中書門下三品，加實封五百戶，固辭不受。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong he was promoted to Minister of Works and concurrent Third Rank at the Secretariat-Chancellery, with an additional five hundred actual fief households, but he firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong era he was promoted to Minister of Works and concurrent Third Rank at the Secretariat-Chancellery, with five hundred additional actual fief households, but he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 未幾，隨例降封為德靜郡王，量減實封二百戶。

translations.literal: Before long, following the usual precedent, he was demoted in rank to Prince of Dejing commandery, with a measured reduction of two hundred actual fief households.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, following the usual precedent, he was demoted to Prince of Dejing commandery, with two hundred households cut from his actual fief.

sentences.zh: 尋拜左散騎常侍，則天遺制令復其所減實封。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed Left Regular Attendant of cavalry, and in Zetian's posthumous edict he was ordered to have his reduced actual fief restored.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was appointed Left Regular Attendant of Cavalry; Zetian's posthumous edict restored the households that had been taken from his fief.

sentences.zh: 初，敬暉等立功後，掌知國政，三思慮其更為己患，而令其子崇訓因安樂公主構誣敬暉等，並流於嶺表而死。

translations.literal: Initially, after Jing Hui and the others had achieved merit and held the reins of state, Sansi feared they would become trouble for him again; he had his son Chongxun, through Princess Anle, fabricate accusations against Jing Hui and the others — all were exiled beyond the Ling range and died.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing Hui and his allies had seized power through their coup, Sansi feared they would threaten him again. Through Princess Anle he had his son Chongxun fabricate charges against Jing Hui and the others; all were exiled beyond the Ling Mountains and died there.

sentences.zh: 自是三思威權日盛，軍國政事，多所參綜。

translations.literal: From this time Sansi's power and authority grew daily; in military and state affairs he participated extensively in decisions.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Sansi's power grew daily, and he meddled extensively in military and civil affairs.

sentences.zh: 敬暉等所斥黜者，皆能引復舊職，令百官復修則天之法。

translations.literal: Those whom Jing Hui and the others had dismissed and degraded, he was able to bring back to their former posts; he ordered the hundred officials to again follow Zetian's laws.
translations.idiomatic: Officials whom Jing Hui and his faction had dismissed, he restored to office; he ordered the bureaucracy to resume Zetian's policies.

sentences.zh: 時人皆言其陰懷篡逆，以比曹孟德、司馬仲達。

translations.literal: People at the time all said he secretly harbored usurpation and rebellion, comparing him to Cao Mengde and Sima Zhongda.
translations.idiomatic: People at the time whispered that he secretly harbored usurpation, comparing him to Cao Cao and Sima Yi.

sentences.zh: 雍州人韋月將、高軫等並上疏言三思父子必為逆亂。

translations.literal: Wei Yuejiang of Yong prefecture, Gao Zhen, and others all submitted memorials stating that Sansi and his son would surely bring rebellion and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuejiang of Yongzhou, Gao Zhen, and others submitted memorials warning that Sansi and his son would surely rebel.

sentences.zh: 三思知而求索其罪。

translations.literal: Sansi learned of this and sought out their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi learned of this and set about finding crimes with which to charge them.

sentences.zh: 有司希旨，奏：「月將坐當棄市，軫配流嶺外」。

translations.literal: The responsible officials, anticipating his wishes, reported: "Yuejiang's offense warrants death by decapitation and display in the market; Zhen is to be matched and exiled beyond the Ling range."
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials, reading his wishes, reported: "Yuejiang's crime warrants execution by decapitation and display; Zhen is to be exiled beyond the Ling Mountains."

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎宋璟執奏云：「月將所犯，不合至死。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Song Jing insistently submitted, saying: "The offense Yuejiang committed does not warrant death.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Song Jing objected in a formal memorial: "Yuejiang's offense does not merit death.

sentences.zh: 」三思怒，竟斥宋璟為外職。

translations.literal: " Sansi was enraged and ultimately expelled Song Jing to an outer post.
translations.idiomatic: " Enraged, Sansi had Song Jing banished to an outer post.

sentences.zh: 三思既猜嫉正士，嘗言「不知何等名作好人，唯有向我好者，是好人耳。

translations.literal: Sansi, now suspicious and jealous of upright men, once said: "I do not know what sort of thing is called a good man — only those who are good to me are good men.
translations.idiomatic: Suspicious and hostile toward upright men, Sansi once said: "I don't know what makes a good man—only those who are good to me are good men.

sentences.zh: 」又與其所親兵部尚書宗楚客、將作大匠宗晉卿、太府卿紀處訥、鴻臚卿甘元柬遞相引致，幹黷時政。

translations.literal: " He also with his intimates — Minister of War Zong Chuke, Grand Master of Works Zong Jinqing, Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury Ji Chunna, and Director of the Court of State Ceremonial Gan Yuanjian — mutually drew one another in, meddling obscenely in affairs of the time.
translations.idiomatic: " He also colluded with his cronies—Minister of War Zong Chuke, Grand Master of Works Zong Jinqing, Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury Ji Chunna, and Director of the Court of State Ceremonial Gan Yuanjian—each pulling the others into power and corrupting the governance of the day.

sentences.zh: 侍御史周利用、冉祖雍，太僕丞李悛，光祿丞宋之遜，監察御史姚紹之等五人，常為其耳目，時人呼為「三思五狗」。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Zhou Liyong, Ran Zuyong, Deputy Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud Li Quan, Deputy Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Song Zhixun, and Investigating Censor Yao Shaozhi — these five — regularly served as his eyes and ears; people of the time called them "Sansi's Five Dogs."
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor Zhou Liyong, Ran Zuyong, Deputy Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud Li Quan, Deputy Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments Song Zhixun, and Investigating Censor Yao Shaozhi—these five served as his eyes and ears; people called them "Sansi's Five Dogs."

sentences.zh: 中宗尋又制：武氏崇恩廟，一依天授時舊禮享祭，其吳陵、順陵，並置官員，皆三思意也。

translations.literal: Zhongzong soon issued another edict: the Wu clan's Temple of Honored Grace was to be sacrificed to according entirely to the old rites of the Tianshou era; Wu Ling and Shun Ling were both given official staff — all of this was Sansi's idea.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong soon issued an edict: the Wu clan's Temple of Honored Grace was to be maintained with sacrifices according to the old Tianshou rites; officials were appointed for Wu Ling and Shun Ling—all at Sansi's instigation.

sentences.zh: 三思既與韋庶人及上官昭容私通，嘗忌節湣太子，又因安樂公主密謀廢黜之。

translations.literal: Sansi, who had been privately carrying on with the Deposed Consort Wei and Shangguan Zhaorong, had long resented Crown Prince Jiemin; moreover, through Princess Anle he secretly plotted to depose him.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi, who was secretly involved with the Deposed Consort Wei and Shangguan Zhaorong, had long resented Crown Prince Jiemin; through Princess Anle he also plotted to have the crown prince deposed.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，太子率羽林大將軍李多祚等，發左右羽林兵，殺三思及其子崇訓於其第，並殺其親黨十餘人。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year the crown prince led General of the Feathered Forest Li Duozuo and others, mobilizing the Left and Right Feathered Forest armies, and killed Sansi and his son Chongxun at their residence — more than ten of their close partisans were also killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year the crown prince, leading General of the Feathered Forest Li Duozuo and others, mobilized the Left and Right Feathered Forest armies and killed Sansi and his son Chongxun at their residence, along with more than ten of their close associates.

sentences.zh: 俄而事變，太子既死，中宗為三思舉哀，廢朝五日，贈太尉，追封梁王，謚曰宣。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward affairs changed; the crown prince having died, Zhongzong held mourning rites for Sansi, canceled court for five days, posthumously granted him Grand Marshal, posthumously enfeoffed him as King of Liang, posthumous name Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Events soon turned: the crown prince was killed, and Zhongzong held mourning rites for Sansi, suspending court for five days. Sansi was posthumously granted Grand Marshal, re-enfeoffed as King of Liang, and given the posthumous name Xuan.

sentences.zh: 安樂公主又以節湣太子首致祭於三思及崇訓靈柩前。

translations.literal: Princess Anle furthermore offered Crown Prince Jiemin's head in sacrifice before the coffins of Sansi and Chongxun.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Anle further placed Crown Prince Jiemin's severed head as an offering before the coffins of Sansi and Chongxun.

sentences.zh: 睿宗踐祚，以三思父子俱有逆節，制令斫棺暴屍，平其墳墓。

translations.literal: When Ruizong ascended the throne, because Sansi and his son both had treasonous conduct, an edict ordered their coffins chopped open and corpses exposed, their tombs leveled.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong took the throne, an edict declared that Sansi and his son had both committed treason; their coffins were broken open, their corpses exposed, and their tombs leveled.

sentences.zh: 三思子　崇訓崇訓，三思第二子也。

translations.literal: Sansi's son Chongxun. Chongxun was Sansi's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi's son Chongxun was Sansi's second son.

sentences.zh: 則天時，封為高陽郡王。

translations.literal: During Zetian's time he was enfeoffed as Prince of Gaoyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During Zetian's reign he was enfeoffed as Prince of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 長安中，尚安樂郡主。

translations.literal: During the Chang'an era he married the Lady of Anle commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an era he married the Lady of Anle.

sentences.zh: 時三思用事於朝，欲寵其禮。

translations.literal: At the time Sansi held power at court and wished to lavish honor on the marriage rites.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi then dominated the court and wished to magnify the wedding ceremony.

sentences.zh: 中宗為太子在東宮，三思宅在天津橋南，自重光門內行親迎禮，歸於其宅。

translations.literal: Zhongzong was crown prince in the Eastern Palace; Sansi's residence was south of Tianjin Bridge — from within Chongguang Gate the bridegroom's welcoming rites were performed, and she was escorted back to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong was still crown prince in the Eastern Palace; Sansi's house stood south of Tianjin Bridge. The bridegroom's welcoming ceremony was conducted from within Chongguang Gate, and the bride was escorted to his residence.

sentences.zh: 三思又令宰臣李嶠、蘇味道，詞人沈佺期、宋之問、徐彥伯、張說、閻朝隱、崔融、崔湜、鄭愔等賦《花燭行》以美之。

translations.literal: Sansi further had chancellors Li Qiao and Su Weidao and poets Shen Quanqi, Song Zhiwen, Xu Yanbo, Zhang Yue, Yan Chaoyin, Cui Rong, Cui Ti, Zheng Yin, and others compose "Song of the Flower Candle" in praise.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi further commissioned chancellors Li Qiao and Su Weidao and poets including Shen Quanqi, Song Zhiwen, Xu Yanbo, Zhang Yue, Yan Chaoyin, Cui Rong, Cui Ti, and Zheng Yin to compose "Song of the Flower Candle" in praise of the wedding.

sentences.zh: 其時張易之、昌宗、宗楚客兄弟貴盛，時假詞於人，皆有新句。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Yizhi, Changzong, and the Zong Chuke brothers were all at the height of noble splendor; they often borrowed others' lines and each had fresh verses.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhang Yizhi, Changzong, and the Zong Chuke brothers were at the height of power and prestige; they often borrowed others' lines, yet each contributed new verses of his own.

sentences.zh: 崇訓授左衛中郎將。

translations.literal: Chongxun was appointed Commandant of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxun was appointed Commandant of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，拜駙馬都尉，遷太常卿，兼左衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong he was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards, transferred to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and concurrently General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shenlong he was made Commandant of the Horse Guards, then transferred to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness while concurrently serving as General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 降封酆國公，仍賜實封五百戶，尋徙封鎬國公。

translations.literal: He was demoted in rank to Duke of Feng state, still granted five hundred actual fief households; shortly afterward his fief was changed to Duke of Hao state.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to Duke of Feng but retained five hundred actual fief households; shortly afterward his title was changed to Duke of Hao.

sentences.zh: 二年，兼太子賓客，攝左衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year he was made concurrent Companion to the Heir Apparent, acting as General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made concurrent Companion to the Heir Apparent, acting as General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 及為節湣太子所殺，優制贈開府儀同三司，追贈魯王，謚曰忠。

translations.literal: When he was killed by Crown Prince Jiemin, a special edict posthumously granted him Honorary Grand General with the Presidency of the Department of State Affairs, posthumously enfeoffed him as King of Lu, posthumous name Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: After Crown Prince Jiemin killed him, a special edict posthumously granted him Honorary Grand General with the Presidency of the Department of State Affairs, enfeoffed him as King of Lu, and gave him the posthumous name Zhong.

sentences.zh: 從祖弟　懿宗懿宗，則天伯父士逸之孫也。

translations.literal: Younger male cousin of the same grandfather Yizong. Yizong was the grandson of Zetian's paternal uncle Shiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Yizong, a younger male cousin on the shared grandfather's side, was the grandson of Zetian's paternal uncle Shiyi.

sentences.zh: 父元忠，高宗時仕至倉部郎中。

translations.literal: His father Yuanzhong during Gaozong's reign rose to Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuanzhong rose during Gaozong's reign to Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 天授年，封士逸為蜀王，懿宗封為河內郡王，歷遷洛州長史、左金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the Tianshou era Shiyi was enfeoffed as King of Shu and Yizong enfeoffed as Prince of Henei commandery; he was repeatedly transferred to Long-term Administrator of Luo prefecture and General of the Left Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianshou era Shiyi was enfeoffed as King of Shu and Yizong as Prince of Henei; Yizong later served as Long-term Administrator of Luozhou and General of the Left Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 萬歲通天年中，契丹賊帥孫萬榮寇河北，命懿宗為大總管討之。

translations.literal: In the Wansui Tongtian era the Khitan bandit chief Sun Wanrong raided Hebei; Yizong was appointed Grand Commander to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wansui Tongtian era the Khitan rebel leader Sun Wanrong invaded Hebei; Yizong was appointed Grand Commander to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 軍次趙州，用聞賊將至冀州，懿宗懼，便欲棄軍而遁。

translations.literal: When the army halted at Zhao prefecture and news came that the bandits were about to reach Ji prefecture, Yizong was afraid and wished at once to abandon the army and flee.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Zhaozhou and word came that the rebels were about to reach Jizhou, Yizong panicked and wanted to abandon his troops and flee.

sentences.zh: 人或謂曰：「賊眾極多，然其軍無輜重，以抄掠為資，若按兵以守，勢必離散，因而擊之。

translations.literal: Someone said to him: "The bandit force is extremely large, yet their army has no baggage train — they rely on raiding for supplies; if you hold your troops and defend, they will surely scatter, and you can strike them then.
translations.idiomatic: Someone advised him: "The rebel force is very large, but they have no baggage train and live by plunder. If you hold your ground, they will inevitably scatter—and then you can strike.

sentences.zh: 可有大功也。

translations.literal: You can achieve great merit.
translations.idiomatic: You can win great merit.

sentences.zh: 」懿宗不聽，遂退據相州，時人嗤其怯懦。

translations.literal: " Yizong would not listen; he retreated and held Xiang prefecture — people of the time mocked him as cowardly.
translations.idiomatic: " Yizong refused to listen. He withdrew to Xiangzhou, and people mocked him for his cowardice.

sentences.zh: 由是賊眾進屠趙州而去。

translations.literal: Thereupon the bandit horde advanced, slaughtered Zhao prefecture, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then advanced, massacred Zhaozhou, and moved on.

sentences.zh: 尋又令懿宗安撫河北諸州。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Yizong was again ordered to pacify the various prefectures of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Yizong was again ordered to pacify the prefectures of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 先是，百姓有脅從賊眾，後得歸來者。

translations.literal: Previously there had been common people who were coerced into following the bandit horde and later were able to return.
translations.idiomatic: By then many commoners who had been forced to follow the rebels were returning home.

sentences.zh: 懿宗以為同反，總殺之。

translations.literal: Yizong regarded them all as having rebelled together and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Yizong treated them all as rebels and had them killed.

sentences.zh: 仍生刳取其膽，後行刑，流血盈前，言笑自若。

translations.literal: He even extracted their gall bladders while they still lived; afterward during the executions, with blood filling the ground before him, he chatted and laughed as if all were normal.
translations.idiomatic: He even cut out their gall bladders while they were still alive; as the executions proceeded and blood pooled at his feet, he chatted and laughed as though nothing were amiss.

sentences.zh: 初。

translations.literal: Previously.
translations.idiomatic: Previously.

sentences.zh: 孫萬榮別帥何阿小攻陷冀州，亦多屠害士女。

translations.literal: Sun Wanrong's subordinate commander He A-xiao captured Ji prefecture and likewise slaughtered many men and women.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Wanrong's lieutenant He A-xiao had captured Jizhou and likewise slaughtered many men and women.

sentences.zh: 至是，時人號懿宗與阿小為兩何，為之語曰：「唯此兩何，殺人最多。

translations.literal: By this time people called Yizong and A-xiao the Two Hes, and a saying about them ran: "Only these Two Hes — they kill the most people.
translations.idiomatic: By then people called Yizong and A-xiao the Two Hes, and a saying went: "Of all who kill, these Two Hes kill the most.

sentences.zh: 」懿宗又自天授已來，嘗受中旨，推鞫制獄，王公大臣，多被陷成其罪，時人以為周興、來俊臣之亞焉。

translations.literal: " Yizong had also, from Tianshou onward, often received secret instructions, conducting interrogations and controlling prisons — kings, dukes, and great ministers were often trapped into crimes by him; people of the time regarded him as second only to Zhou Xing and Lai Junchen.
translations.idiomatic: " Yizong had also, since the Tianshou era, often received secret orders to conduct interrogations and control the prisons; kings, dukes, and great ministers were frequently framed and convicted through his hand. People regarded him as second only to Zhou Xing and Lai Junchen.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，隨例降爵，封耿國公，累轉懷州刺史，尋卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, following the usual precedent he was demoted in rank and enfeoffed as Duke of Geng state; he was repeatedly transferred to Prefect of Huai prefecture and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong era he was demoted by precedent to Duke of Geng, later served as Prefect of Huaizhou, and soon died.

sentences.zh: 從父弟　攸暨攸暨，則天伯父士讓孫也。

translations.literal: Younger male cousin of the same grandfather Youji. Youji was the grandson of Zetian's paternal uncle Shirang.
translations.idiomatic: Youji, a younger male cousin on the shared grandfather's side, was the grandson of Zetian's paternal uncle Shirang.

sentences.zh: 天授中，封士讓為楚王，攸暨封千乘郡王。

translations.literal: During Tianshou, Shirang was enfeoffed as King of Chu and Youji enfeoffed as Prince of Qiansheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianshou, Shirang was enfeoffed as King of Chu and Youji as Prince of Qiansheng.

sentences.zh: 賜爵實封三百戶。

translations.literal: He was granted noble rank with an actual fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He received a noble title with an actual fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 兄攸寧為建昌郡王，實封四百戶。

translations.literal: His elder brother Youning was Prince of Jianchang commandery with an actual fief of four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Youning was Prince of Jianchang with an actual fief of four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 攸寧歷遷鳳閣侍郎、納言、冬官尚書，病卒。

translations.literal: Youning was repeatedly transferred to Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion, Remonstrating Secretary, and Minister of the Winter Office; he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Youning served in turn as Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion, Remonstrating Secretary, and Minister of the Winter Office, and died of illness.

sentences.zh: 攸暨初為右衛中郎將，尚太平公主，授駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Youji was initially Commandant of the Right Guard; he married Princess Taiping and was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Youji was first Commandant of the Right Guard; he married Princess Taiping and was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards.

sentences.zh: 累遷右衛將軍，進封定王，又加實封三百戶。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to General of the Right Guard, advanced in rank to King Ding, with an additional three hundred actual fief households.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General of the Right Guard, was advanced to King Ding, and received three hundred additional actual fief households.

sentences.zh: 俄又改安定郡王，歷遷司禮卿、左散騎常侍，加特進。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was changed to Prince of Anding commandery; he was repeatedly transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Left Regular Attendant of cavalry, and given Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward his title was changed to Prince of Anding; he served as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Left Regular Attendant of Cavalry, and was granted Special Advancement.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，拜司徒，復封定王，實封滿一千戶，固辭不拜。

translations.literal: During Shenlong he was appointed Minister of Education, again enfeoffed as King Ding, his actual fief reaching one thousand households — he firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong era he was appointed Minister of Education and again enfeoffed as King Ding with an actual fief of one thousand households, but he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 尋而隨例降封樂壽郡王，拜右散騎常侍，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, following the usual precedent, he was demoted to Prince of Leshou commandery, appointed Right Regular Attendant of cavalry, and given Honorary Grand General with the Presidency of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, following precedent, he was demoted to Prince of Leshou, appointed Right Regular Attendant of Cavalry, and granted Honorary Grand General with the Presidency of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 延秀等誅後，又降封楚國公。

translations.literal: After Yanxiu and the others were executed, he was again demoted to Duke of Chu state.
translations.idiomatic: After Yanxiu and the others were executed, he was demoted again to Duke of Chu.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太尉、并州大都督，追封定王。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously appointed Grand Commandant and Great Protector-General of Bingzhou; posthumously enfeoffed as King Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed Grand Commandant and Great Protector-General of Bingzhou, with posthumous enfeoffment as King Ding.

sentences.zh: 尋以公主謀逆，令平毀其墓。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, because the princess plotted rebellion, an order was issued to level and destroy his tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, when the princess plotted rebellion, the court ordered his tomb leveled and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 太平公主者，高宗少女也。

translations.literal: Princess Taiping was the youngest daughter of Emperor Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Taiping was Emperor Gaozong's youngest daughter.

sentences.zh: 以則天所生，特承恩寵。

translations.literal: Because she was born to Empress Zetian, she received special imperial favor and indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: As Zetian's own daughter, she enjoyed exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 初，永隆年降駙馬薛紹。

translations.literal: Initially, in the Yonglong era she was married to Imperial Son-in-law Xue Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, in the Yonglong era, she married Imperial Son-in-law Xue Shao.

sentences.zh: 紹，垂拱中被誣告與諸王連謀伏誅，則天私殺攸暨之妻以配主焉。

translations.literal: Shao, during Chuihong, was falsely accused of plotting with various princes and was executed; Zetian secretly killed Youji's wife to give her to the princess as spouse.
translations.idiomatic: During Chuihong, Shao was falsely accused of plotting with various princes and executed; Zetian secretly had Youji's wife killed and gave her to the princess as a new match.

sentences.zh: 公主豐碩，方額廣頤，多權略，則天以為類己，每預謀議，宮禁嚴峻，事不令泄。

translations.literal: The princess was full-bodied, with square forehead and broad cheeks; skilled in stratagems—Zetian thought her like herself; she joined every plot and counsel; palace prohibitions were severe, affairs were not allowed to leak.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was imposing in build, with a square forehead and broad cheeks, and she was adept at intrigue. Zetian saw her as a kindred spirit and included her in every plot; palace security was tight and nothing was permitted to leak out.

sentences.zh: 公主亦畏懼自檢，但崇飾邸第。

translations.literal: The princess also feared and examined herself, only adorning her mansion splendidly.
translations.idiomatic: The princess, for her part, lived in cautious restraint and confined herself to lavishly outfitting her mansion.

sentences.zh: 二十餘年，天下獨有太平一公主，父為帝，母為后，夫為親王，子為郡王，貴盛無比。

translations.literal: For more than twenty years, under Heaven there was only Princess Taiping—for whom father was emperor, mother was empress, husband was imperial prince, and sons were commandery princes—nobility and splendor without peer.
translations.idiomatic: For more than twenty years, Princess Taiping alone in the empire could claim an emperor for a father, an empress for a mother, an imperial prince for a husband, and commandery princes for sons—wealth and rank beyond compare.

sentences.zh: 永淳已前朝制，親王食實封八百戶，有至一千戶；

translations.literal: Before Yongchun, under court regulations, imperial princes received actual fiefs of eight hundred households, some reaching one thousand;
translations.idiomatic: Before Yongchun, court custom granted imperial princes actual fiefs of eight hundred households, with some reaching one thousand;

sentences.zh: 公主出降三百戶，公主加五十戶。

translations.literal: princesses upon marriage three hundred households, with an additional fifty for being princess.
translations.idiomatic: princesses upon marriage received three hundred households, with an additional fifty for the princess title itself.

sentences.zh: 太平食湯沐之邑一千二百戶，聖歷初加至三千戶。

translations.literal: Taiping received a bathing-fief of one thousand two hundred households; at the beginning of Shenglì it was increased to three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping held a ceremonial fief of twelve hundred households; at the start of Shenglì this rose to three thousand.

sentences.zh: ，預誅張易之謀有功，進號鎮國太平公主，相王加號安國相王，並食實封通前五千戶，賞賜不可勝紀。

translations.literal: , for meritorious participation in the plot to execute Zhang Yizhi, her title was advanced to "Pacifying the Realm" Princess Taiping; the Prince of Xiang received the additional title "Pacifying the State" Prince of Xiang; both received actual fiefs totaling five thousand households including prior grants; rewards and gifts beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: For her part in the successful plot against Zhang Yizhi, her title was elevated to Pacifying-the-Realm Princess Taiping, and the Prince of Xiang was styled Pacifying-the-State Prince of Xiang; together they received actual fiefs of five thousand households counting earlier grants, and rewards beyond tallying.

sentences.zh: 公主孽氏二男二女，武氏二男一女，並食實封。

translations.literal: The princess's children by concubines—two sons and two daughters—and Wu-clan children—two sons and one daughter—all received actual fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: The princess's two sons and two daughters by concubines, together with two Wu-clan sons and one daughter, all held actual fiefs.

sentences.zh: 又相王、衛王重俊、成王千里宅，遣衛士宿衛，環其所居，十步置一仗舍，持兵巡僥，同於宮禁。

translations.literal: Furthermore, at the mansions of the Prince of Xiang, Prince Wei Chongjun, and Prince Cheng Qianli, guards were dispatched to lodge overnight, encircling their residences; every ten paces a sentry booth was set up, armed patrols making rounds—as in the palace precincts.
translations.idiomatic: Guards were also posted overnight at the mansions of the Prince of Xiang, Prince Wei Chongjun, and Prince Cheng Qianli, encircling their residences with a sentry booth every ten paces and armed patrols—matching palace security.

sentences.zh: 太平、長寧、安樂三公主，置鋪一如親王。

translations.literal: The three princesses Taiping, Changning, and Anle had guard stations set up like imperial princes.
translations.idiomatic: Princesses Taiping, Changning, and Anle were given guard stations on the same model as imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，置公主府。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, princesses' bureaus were established.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year, official princess households were established.

sentences.zh: ，公主男崇簡、崇敏、崇行，同授三品，與漁陽王兄弟四人同制。

translations.literal: , the princess's sons Chongjian, Chongmin, and Chongxing were all appointed to the third rank together, on the same terms as the four brothers of the Prince of Yuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Her sons Chongjian, Chongmin, and Chongxing were all given third rank together, under the same arrangement as the four Yuyang princes.

sentences.zh: 時中宗仁善，韋后、上官昭容用事禁中，皆以為智謀不及公主，甚憚之。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Zhongzong was benevolent and mild; Empress Wei and Shangguan Zhaorong wielded power within the palace—they all considered their wisdom and schemes inferior to the princess's and greatly feared her.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong was mild by nature; Empress Wei and Shangguan Zhaorong held sway inside the palace, but both judged themselves no match for the princess in wit and scheme, and feared her deeply.

sentences.zh: 公主日益豪橫，進達朝士，多至大官，詞人後進造其門者，或有貧窘，則遺之金帛，士亦翕然稱之。

translations.literal: The princess grew daily more domineering; she advanced court officials, many reaching high office; literati and rising talents who came to her gate—if any were poor and straitened—she would give them gold and silk; the gentlemen also unanimously praised her.
translations.idiomatic: The princess grew ever more overbearing, advancing court officials—many to high office. When poets and rising talents visited her gate, the needy among them received gold and silk, and men of letters spoke of her with one voice in praise.

sentences.zh: 及六月，韋后作逆稱制，偽尊溫王。

translations.literal: When the sixth month came, Empress Wei staged rebellion and assumed imperial authority, falsely elevating the Prince of Wen.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Empress Wei rebelled, assumed regency, and set up the Prince of Wen as a puppet ruler.

sentences.zh: 玄宗居臨淄邸，憤之，將清內難。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong resided at the Linzi mansion, enraged at this, and prepared to settle the internal crisis.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong, lodged at the Linzi mansion, burned with anger and prepared to resolve the crisis within the palace.

sentences.zh: 公主又預其謀，令男崇簡從之。

translations.literal: The princess again joined their plot, ordering her son Chongjian to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: The princess joined the plot as well, sending her son Chongjian to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 及立溫王，數日，天下之心歸於相府，難為其議。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Wen was enthroned, within days the hearts of the realm turned to the Prince of Xiang's mansion, and the arrangement was hard to maintain.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Prince of Wen was installed, within days public sentiment rallied to the Prince of Xiang, and the arrangement became untenable.

sentences.zh: 公主入啟幼主，以王室多故，資於長君，乃提下幼主，因與玄宗、大臣尊立睿宗。

translations.literal: The princess entered to inform the young ruler that, with the royal house beset by many troubles, reliance on an elder lord was needed; she then led the young ruler down, and together with Xuanzong and the chief ministers honored and enthroned Emperor Ruizong.
translations.idiomatic: The princess went in to advise the young emperor that the royal house was in turmoil and needed an elder, steady hand; she brought the boy down from the throne, and with Xuanzong and the chief ministers installed Ruizong.

sentences.zh: 公主頻著大勛，益尊重，乃加實封五千戶，通前滿一萬戶。

translations.literal: The princess repeatedly earned great merit and grew ever more honored; she was given an additional five thousand actual fief households, totaling ten thousand with previous grants.
translations.idiomatic: Having earned great merit repeatedly, the princess rose still higher in honor and received five thousand additional actual fief households, bringing her total to ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 公主子崇行、崇敏、崇簡三人，封異姓王；

translations.literal: The princess's three sons Chongxing, Chongmin, and Chongjian were enfeoffed as kings of a non-imperial surname;
translations.idiomatic: Her three sons—Chongxing, Chongmin, and Chongjian—were enfeoffed as kings of surname other than Li;

sentences.zh: 崇行國子祭酒，四人九卿三品。

translations.literal: Chongxing as Director of the National University; four men held nine-minister and third-rank posts.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxing became Director of the National University; four of them held third-rank posts among the Nine Ministers.

sentences.zh: 每入奏事，坐語移時，所言皆聽。

translations.literal: Whenever she entered to report affairs, she would sit and converse for a long stretch; whatever she said was heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Each time she came in to report, she would sit in audience for hours, and whatever she proposed was accepted.

sentences.zh: 薦人或驟歷清職，或至南北衙將相，權移人主。

translations.literal: Those she recommended might suddenly rise through pure offices, or reach generals and chancellors of the northern and southern bureaus—power shifted from the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Her recommendations could vault men into clean, high offices or into the chancellors and generals of both bureaus—the locus of power shifted away from the throne.

sentences.zh: 軍國大政，事必參決，如不朝謁，則宰臣就第議其可否。

translations.literal: On great affairs of army and state she had to be consulted before decisions; if she did not attend court, chancellors would go to her mansion to debate what should or should not be done.
translations.idiomatic: On matters of army and state she had to be consulted; when she skipped court, chancellors came to her mansion to debate policy with her.

sentences.zh: 公主由是滋驕，田園遍於近甸膏腴，而市易造作器物，吳、蜀、嶺南供送，相屬於路。

translations.literal: The princess thereby grew ever more arrogant; her estates and gardens spread throughout the fat lands near the capital, while for trade and crafted goods Wu, Shu, and Lingnan sent tribute in succession along the roads.
translations.idiomatic: From this the princess grew still more arrogant. Her estates spread across the fertile fields near the capital; for commerce and manufactured luxuries, Wu, Shu, and Lingnan sent goods in an unbroken stream along the roads.

sentences.zh: 綺疏寶帳，音樂輿乘，同於宮掖。

translations.literal: Latticed silk windows and jeweled canopies, music and carriages—equal to the palace women's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Carved silk screens, jeweled canopies, music, and equipages matched the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 侍兒披羅綺，常數百人，蒼頭監嫗，必盈千數。

translations.literal: Attendant girls clad in gauze and brocade, often numbering in the hundreds; male and female household stewards, necessarily exceeding a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of maids in gauze and brocade were always in attendance; male and female servants numbered more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 外州供狗馬玩好滋味，不可紀極。

translations.literal: Outer provinces supplied dogs, horses, curios, delicacies, and flavors beyond all reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Outlying provinces sent dogs, horses, curios, and delicacies in quantities beyond count.

sentences.zh: 有胡僧惠範，家富於財寶，善事權貴，公主與之私，奏為聖善寺主，加三品，封公，殖貨流於江劍。

translations.literal: There was the foreign monk Huifan, whose household overflowed with treasure; skilled at serving the powerful, the princess had a secret affair with him; he was memorialized to be abbot of Shengshan Temple, raised to third rank, enfeoffed as duke; his profiteering flowed through Jiang and Jian.
translations.idiomatic: A foreign monk named Huifan, immensely wealthy, cultivated the powerful; the princess took him as a lover and had him made abbot of Shengshan Temple, raised to third rank and enfeoffed as duke, while his trading interests spread through the Jiang and Jian regions.

sentences.zh: 公主懼玄宗英武，乃連結將相，專謀異計。

translations.literal: The princess feared Xuanzong's martial prowess; she then linked chiefs and generals, plotting exclusive alternate designs.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Xuanzong's martial spirit, the princess cultivated ties with chiefs and generals and plotted against him.

sentences.zh: 其時宰相七人，五出公主門，常元楷、李慈掌禁兵，常私謁公主。

translations.literal: At that time among seven chancellors, five came from the princess's circle; Chang Yuankai and Li Ci controlled the forbidden guard and often paid private calls on the princess.
translations.idiomatic: Of the seven chancellors, five were her clients; Chang Yuankai and Li Ci commanded the palace guard and visited her privately on a regular basis.

sentences.zh: 七月，玄宗在武德殿，事漸危逼，乃勒兵誅其黨竇懷貞、蕭至忠、岑羲等，公主遽入山寺，數日方出，賜死於家。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Xuanzong was at Wude Hall; as the affair grew perilously pressing, he mustered troops and executed her faction—Dou HuaiZhen, Xiao Zhizhong, Cen Xi, and others; the princess hastened into a mountain monastery, emerged only after several days, and was ordered to die at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, as matters at Wude Hall grew dangerously urgent, Xuanzong moved troops and executed her allies—Dou HuaiZhen, Xiao Zhizhong, Cen Xi, and others. The princess fled into a mountain monastery, did not emerge for several days, and was then granted death in her own house.

sentences.zh: 公主諸子及黨與死者數十人。

translations.literal: The princess's sons and factional associates who died numbered dozens.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of the princess's sons and associates perished with her.

sentences.zh: 籍其家，財貨山積，珍奇寶物，侔於御府，馬牧羊牧田園質庫，數年徵斂不盡。

translations.literal: Her household was confiscated; goods piled like mountains, rare treasures rivaling the imperial storehouse; horses, sheep, herds, estates, pawn-shops—for years the levies could not be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Her property was confiscated: wealth heaped like a mountain, curios rivaling the imperial treasury; horses, flocks, estates, and pawn offices yielded revenue for years that could not be fully collected.

sentences.zh: 惠範家產亦數十萬貫。

translations.literal: Huifan's household assets also amounted to several hundred thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Huifan's estate as well came to several hundred thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 惟良子　攸緒攸緒，惟良子也。

translations.literal: Son of Weiliang: Youxu. Youxu was Weiliang's son.
translations.idiomatic: Youxu, son of Weiliang, was Weiliang's son.

sentences.zh: 少有志行。

translations.literal: From youth he had aspiration and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was known for integrity and purpose.

sentences.zh: 天授中封安平郡王，歷遷殿中監，出為揚州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: During Tianshou he was enfeoffed Prince of Anping commandery; successively promoted to Director of the Palace Administration; sent out as Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou Metropolitan Protectorate.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianshou he was enfeoffed Prince of Anping, rose to Director of the Palace Administration, and was appointed Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou Metropolitan Protectorate.

sentences.zh: 聖歷中，棄官隱於嵩山，以琴書藥餌為務。

translations.literal: During Shenglì, he abandoned office and hid on Mount Song, making zither, books, and medicinal elixirs his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: During Shenglì he resigned his post and retired to Mount Song, devoting himself to the zither, books, and medicinal alchemy.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，以車安備禮徵之，降書曰：

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong took the throne, he was summoned with carriage, comforts, and full ceremony; an imperial letter was issued, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong came to the throne, he was summoned with proper carriage and ceremonial honors; an imperial letter went out, saying:

sentences.zh: 攸緒應召至都，授太子賓客。

translations.literal: Youxu answered the summons and came to the capital; he was appointed Counselor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Youxu answered the summons and came to the capital, where he was appointed Counselor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋請歸嵩山，制從之，令京官五品已上餞送於定鼎門外。

translations.literal: Shortly he requested return to Mount Song; an edict granted it, ordering capital officials of fifth rank and above to give a farewell send-off outside Dingding Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked to return to Mount Song; the throne assented and ordered capital officials of fifth rank and above to escort him to a farewell outside Dingding Gate.

sentences.zh: 及三思、延秀等構逆，諸武多坐誅戮，唯攸緒以隱居不預其禍，時論美之。

translations.literal: When Sansi, Yanxiu, and others hatched rebellion, many of the Wu clan suffered execution; only Youxu, through reclusion, did not share their calamity—contemporary opinion praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When Sansi, Yanxiu, and others plotted treason and most of the Wu clan were executed, Youxu alone escaped calamity through his reclusion, and public opinion applauded him.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，又降敕曰：「頃以賊臣結黨，后族擅權，扇動宮闈，肆行鴆毒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, another edict was issued: "Recently, villainous ministers formed factions, the empress's clan seized power, stirred the inner palace, and wantonly practiced poisonous murder.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong took the throne, another edict proclaimed: "Lately villainous ministers formed cliques, the empress's kin seized power, stirred turmoil in the inner palace, and poison ran freely.

sentences.zh: 靈祇所感，奸惡伏誅；

translations.literal: Moved by spirits and gods, the wicked were struck down and executed;
translations.idiomatic: Moved by the spirits, the wicked have been brought low and executed;

sentences.zh: 今得宗社乂安，天地交泰。

translations.literal: Now the altars of state are tranquil and secure, Heaven and Earth are in mutual harmony.
translations.idiomatic: the altars of state are at peace and Heaven and Earth are in harmony again.

sentences.zh: 卿久厭簪紱，早慕林泉，守道不回，見幾而作，興言高尚，有足嘉稱。

translations.literal: You have long wearied of official insignia, early sought forests and springs, held the Way without turning back, acted upon seeing the moment, and when one speaks of lofty withdrawal, there is enough to merit praise.
translations.idiomatic: You long ago wearied of rank and ribbon, and early turned toward mountain and stream; you held to the Way without wavering, acted when the moment was right, and your lofty withdrawal deserves every praise.

sentences.zh: 但怒用不遷，罪無相及，為善有驗，卿之謂與！

translations.literal: But though the wicked were punished without exception, guilt does not extend by association; virtue has its proof—you are the living example!
translations.idiomatic: Though offenders were punished without leniency, guilt does not extend by association; virtue brings its own reward—and you are proof of it!

sentences.zh: 或慮驚疑，故令慰謝。

translations.literal: Perhaps fearing alarm and doubt, therefore an order was issued to send reassurance.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing you might be alarmed or unsettled, we send this message of reassurance.

sentences.zh: 」其見重如此。

translations.literal: " He was esteemed to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 尋徵為太子賓客，不就。

translations.literal: Shortly he was summoned as Counselor to the Heir Apparent; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned again as Counselor to the Heir Apparent but declined.

sentences.zh: ，攸緒又請就廬山居止，制不許。

translations.literal: , Youxu again requested to dwell on Mount Lu; an edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Youxu then asked to take up residence on Mount Lu, but the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 仍令州縣數加存問，不令外人侵擾。

translations.literal: Still ordered the prefectures and counties repeatedly to send inquiries, not permitting outsiders to harass him.
translations.idiomatic: The court still ordered local officials to inquire after him regularly and forbade outsiders to disturb him.

sentences.zh: 十一年卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he died, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he died, at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 薛懷義薛懷義者，京兆鄠縣人，本姓馮，名小寶。

translations.literal: Xue Huaiyi. Xue Huaiyi was a man of Hu County in Jingzhao; his original surname was Feng and his given name Xiaobao.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Huaiyi was a native of Hu County in Jingzhao; his original surname was Feng and his given name Xiaobao.

sentences.zh: 以鬻臺貨為業，偉形神，有膂力，為市於洛陽，得幸於千金公主侍兒。

translations.literal: He made his living selling goods at market stalls; his form and spirit were imposing and he had great physical strength; trading in Luoyang, he won favor with a maid of Princess Qianjin.
translations.idiomatic: He made his living as a market trader; imposing in build and strong of limb, he did business in Luoyang and won the favor of a maid in Princess Qianjin's household.

sentences.zh: 公主知之，入宮言曰：「小寶有非常材用，可以近侍。

translations.literal: The princess learned of it, entered the palace and said: "Xiaobao has extraordinary talent and ability and can serve in close attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When the princess learned of this, she went into the palace and said, "Xiaobao has extraordinary gifts and is fit for close attendance.

sentences.zh: 」因得召見，恩遇日深。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was summoned to an audience, and imperial favor grew deeper day by day.
translations.idiomatic: " He was summoned to audience, and favor deepened day by day.

sentences.zh: 則天欲隱其跡，便於出入禁中，乃度為僧。

translations.literal: Zetian wished to conceal his tracks and facilitate his coming and going within the forbidden palace; she therefore ordained him as a monk.
translations.idiomatic: Zetian wished to conceal his movements and ease his access to the inner palace, so she had him ordained as a monk.

sentences.zh: 又以懷義非士族，乃改姓薛，令與太平公主婿薛紹合族，令紹以季父事之。

translations.literal: Also, because Huaiyi was not of the gentry clans, she changed his surname to Xue, had him join clan with Princess Taiping's son-in-law Xue Shao, and ordered Shao to treat him as a younger paternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Because Huaiyi was not of the gentry, she changed his surname to Xue, had him incorporated into the clan of Princess Taiping's son-in-law Xue Shao, and ordered Shao to treat him as a younger paternal uncle.

sentences.zh: 自是與洛陽大德僧法明、處一、惠儼、稜行、感德、感知、靜軌、宣政等在內道場念誦。

translations.literal: From then on, together with the great virtuous monks of Luoyang—Faming, Chuyi, Huiyan, Lengxing, Gande, GanZhi, Jinggui, and Xuanzheng—he recited sutras in the inner dharma hall.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he joined the great Luoyang monks Faming, Chuyi, Huiyan, Lengxing, Gande, GanZhi, Jinggui, and Xuanzheng in sutra recitation at the inner dharma hall.

sentences.zh: 懷義出入乘廄馬，中官侍從，諸武朝貴，匍匐禮謁，人間呼為薛師。

translations.literal: Huaiyi went in and out riding stable horses, with eunuchs attending; Wu clansmen and court nobles prostrated themselves in obeisance; among the people he was called Master Xue.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyi rode imperial stable horses when he went abroad, attended by eunuchs; Wu clansmen and court grandees prostrated themselves before him, and people called him Master Xue.

sentences.zh: 垂拱初，說則天於故洛陽城西修故白馬寺，懷義自護作。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chuihong, he persuaded Zetian to restore the old White Horse Temple west of the former Luoyang city; Huaiyi personally supervised the construction.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Chuihong he persuaded Zetian to restore the old White Horse Temple west of Luoyang, and Huaiyi personally supervised the work.

sentences.zh: 寺成，自為寺主。

translations.literal: When the temple was completed, he made himself its abbot.
translations.idiomatic: When the temple was finished, he installed himself as abbot.

sentences.zh: 頗恃恩狂蹶，其下犯法，人不敢言。

translations.literal: He relied greatly on favor and was wildly arrogant; when his subordinates violated the law, no one dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: He grew arrogant on imperial favor; when his followers broke the law, no one dared report it.

sentences.zh: 右臺御史馮思勖屢以法劾之；

translations.literal: Right Censorate Investigating Censor Feng Sijiu repeatedly impeached him according to law;
translations.idiomatic: Right Censorate Investigating Censor Feng Sijiu repeatedly impeached him under the law;

sentences.zh: 懷義遇勖於途，令從者毆之，幾死。

translations.literal: Huaiyi encountered Sijiu on the road and ordered his followers to beat him; he nearly died.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyi met Sijiu on the road and had his followers beat him nearly to death.

sentences.zh: 又於建春門內敬愛寺別造殿宇，改名佛授記寺。

translations.literal: He also separately built halls within Jing'ai Temple inside Jianchun Gate, renaming it Foshouji Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He also built separate halls within Jing'ai Temple inside Jianchun Gate and renamed it Foshouji Temple.

sentences.zh: ，拆乾元殿，於其地造明堂，懷義充使督作。

translations.literal: , the Qianyuan Hall was demolished and the Bright Hall was built on its site; Huaiyi served as commissioner supervising the work.
translations.idiomatic: The Qianyuan Hall was demolished and the Bright Hall erected on the site, with Huaiyi appointed commissioner to supervise construction.

sentences.zh: 凡役數萬人，曳一大木千人，置號頭，頭一㘚，千人齊和。

translations.literal: In all tens of thousands of laborers were conscripted; to drag one great timber required a thousand men; work-chant leaders were appointed—when the leader gave one shout, a thousand men responded in chorus.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of laborers were pressed into service; a thousand men were needed to haul each great timber, with chant leaders appointed so that one call from the leader brought a thousand voices in unison.

sentences.zh: 明堂大屋凡三層，計高二百尺。

translations.literal: The Bright Hall's great structure had three tiers in all, totaling two hundred feet in height.
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Hall rose in three tiers to a height of two hundred feet.

sentences.zh: 又於明堂北起天堂，廣袤亞於明堂。

translations.literal: A Heavenly Hall was also raised north of the Bright Hall, its breadth and length slightly less than the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Bright Hall they also raised the Heavenly Hall, slightly smaller in breadth and length.

sentences.zh: 懷義以功拜左威衛大將軍，封梁國公。

translations.literal: Huaiyi, for his merit, was appointed General of the Left Weiwu Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: For this work Huaiyi was appointed General of the Left Weiwu Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 永昌中，突厥默啜犯邊，以懷義為清平道大總管，率軍擊之，至單於臺，刻石紀功而還。

translations.literal: During Yongchang, the Türk Mo-ch'o raided the frontier; Huaiyi was made Grand Commander of the Qingping Circuit, led troops to strike him, reached Chanyu Terrace, carved stone to record his merit, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongchang, when the Türk Mo-ch'o raided the frontier, Huaiyi was made Grand Commander of the Qingping Circuit, led troops against him, reached Chanyu Terrace, carved a stone record of his achievement, and returned.

sentences.zh: 加輔國大將軍，進右衛大將軍，改封鄂國公、柱國，賜帛二千段。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title Assistant State General, advanced to General of the Right Guard, changed in enfeoffment to Duke of E and Pillar of State, and granted two thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made Assistant State General and General of the Right Guard, enfeoffed as Duke of E and Pillar of State, and granted two thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 懷義與法明等造《大雲經》，陳符命，言則天是彌勒下生，作閻浮提主，唐氏合微。

translations.literal: Huaiyi together with Faming and others fabricated the Great Cloud Sutra, setting forth portents, saying Zetian was Maitreya descended, ruler of Jambudvīpa, and that the Tang house was destined to wane.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyi and Faming and others fabricated the Great Cloud Sutra, proclaiming portents that Zetian was Maitreya reborn, sovereign of Jambudvīpa, and that the Tang line was fated to decline.

sentences.zh: 故則天革命稱周，懷義與法明等九人並封縣公，賜物有差，皆賜紫袈娑、銀龜袋。

translations.literal: Therefore Zetian changed the dynasty and styled herself Zhou; Huaiyi and Faming and nine others were all enfeoffed as commandery dukes, gifts granted in varying measure, all given purple monastic robes and silver tortoise pouches.
translations.idiomatic: When Zetian changed the dynasty and styled herself Zhou, Huaiyi, Faming, and seven others—all nine of them—were enfeoffed as commandery dukes, given gifts in varying measure, and awarded purple monastic robes and silver tortoise pouches.

sentences.zh: 其偽《大雲經》頒於天下寺，各藏一本，令升高座講說。

translations.literal: The spurious Great Cloud Sutra was promulgated to temples throughout the realm; each was to keep one copy and was ordered to ascend the high seat and expound it.
translations.idiomatic: The forged Great Cloud Sutra was distributed to every temple in the realm, each to keep one copy and expound it from the high seat.

sentences.zh: 則天將革命，誅殺宗屬諸王，唯千金公主以巧媚善進奉獨存；

translations.literal: When Zetian was about to change the dynasty, she executed imperial clansmen and various princes; only Princess Qianjin, through artful flattery and skillful offerings, alone survived;
translations.idiomatic: As Zetian prepared to change the dynasty, she executed the imperial clansmen and princes; only Princess Qianjin survived, through artful flattery and lavish offerings;

sentences.zh: 抗疏請以則天為母，因得曲加恩寵，改邑號為延安大長公主，加實封，賜姓武氏。

translations.literal: she submitted a memorial requesting that Zetian be treated as her mother; thereby she received special added favor, her fief title was changed to Great Princess of Yan'an, actual fief was added, and she was granted the surname Wu.
translations.idiomatic: she submitted a memorial asking to take Zetian as her mother, and thereby won special favor: her title was changed to Great Princess of Yan'an, her actual fief was increased, and she was granted the surname Wu.

sentences.zh: 以子克乂娶魏王武承嗣女，內門參問，不限早晚，見則盡歡。

translations.literal: Because her son Keyi married the daughter of Prince Wei Wu Chengsi, visits at the inner gate were unrestricted as to time; whenever they met, they enjoyed themselves to the full.
translations.idiomatic: Her son Keyi married the daughter of Prince Wei Wu Chengsi, and visits at the inner gate were permitted at any hour; whenever they met, the revelry ran its full course.

sentences.zh: ，默啜復犯塞，又以懷義為代北道行軍大總管，以李多祚、蘇宏暉為將。

translations.literal: , Mo-ch'o again raided the frontier passes; Huaiyi was again made Grand Military Commander of the Daibei Circuit, with Li Duozuo and Su Honghui as generals.
translations.idiomatic: When Mo-ch'o again raided the frontier, Huaiyi was again made Grand Military Commander of the Daibei Circuit, with Li Duozuo and Su Honghui as his generals.

sentences.zh: 未行，改朔方道行軍大總管，以內史李昭德為行軍長史，鳳閣侍郎、平章事蘇味道為行軍司馬，契苾明、曹仁師、沙咤忠義等十八將軍以討之。

translations.literal: Before he set out, he was changed to Grand Military Commander of the Shuofang Circuit; Palace Secretary Li Zhaode was made campaign chief administrator, Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and Grand Councilor Su Weidao was made campaign vice marshal, and eighteen generals including Qibi Ming, Cao Renshi, and Shazha Zhongyi were sent to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Before he marched, his appointment was changed to Grand Military Commander of the Shuofang Circuit, with Palace Secretary Li Zhaode as campaign chief administrator, Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and Grand Councilor Su Weidao as campaign vice marshal, and eighteen generals including Qibi Ming, Cao Renshi, and Shazha Zhongyi to subdue the enemy.

sentences.zh: 未行虜退，乃止。

translations.literal: Before he set out the barbarians withdrew, and the campaign was halted.
translations.idiomatic: Before the army marched, the enemy withdrew, and the campaign was called off.

sentences.zh: 懷義後厭入宮中，多居白馬寺，刺血畫大像，選有膂力白丁度為僧，數滿千人。

translations.literal: Later Huaiyi grew weary of entering the palace and mostly stayed at White Horse Temple; he pricked his blood to paint a great image, selected strong commoners and ordained them as monks, until the number reached a full thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyi later grew weary of the palace and spent most of his time at White Horse Temple, pricking his blood to paint a great image and ordaining strong commoners as monks until their number reached a thousand.

sentences.zh: 侍御史周矩疑其奸，奏請劾之，不許。

translations.literal: Attending Censor Zhou Ju suspected his misconduct and memorialized requesting impeachment; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Attending Censor Zhou Ju suspected wrongdoing and memorialized for an investigation, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 固請之，則天曰：「卿且退，朕即令去。

translations.literal: He firmly pressed the request; Zetian said: "Withdraw for now; I shall immediately have him come.
translations.idiomatic: When he pressed the matter, Zetian said, "Withdraw for now—I shall have him come to you at once.

sentences.zh: 」矩至臺，薛師亦至，乘馬蹋階而下，便坦腹於床。

translations.literal: " When Ju reached the censorate, Master Xue also arrived; riding his horse he trampled down the steps, then lay bare-bellied on a couch.
translations.idiomatic: Ju returned to the censorate, and Master Xue arrived as well—riding his horse down the steps and then sprawling bare-bellied on a couch.

sentences.zh: 矩召臺吏，將按之，遽乘馬而去。

translations.literal: Ju summoned censorate clerks, about to investigate him, but he suddenly mounted his horse and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Ju summoned the censorate clerks to investigate, but Huaiyi suddenly mounted his horse and rode off.

sentences.zh: 矩具以聞，則天曰：「此道人風病，不可苦問。

translations.literal: Ju reported the full matter; Zetian said: "This monk has wind disorder; he cannot be harshly questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Ju reported everything; Zetian said, "This monk suffers from wind disorder and cannot be pressed with hard questioning.

sentences.zh: 所度僧任卿勘當。

translations.literal: The monks he ordained—leave investigation and adjudication to you.
translations.idiomatic: As for the monks he ordained, you may investigate and adjudicate as you see fit.

sentences.zh: 」矩按之，窮其狀以聞，諸僧悉配遠州。

translations.literal: " Ju investigated them, exhaustively reported their circumstances, and all the monks were banished to distant prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Ju investigated, reported the full findings, and all the monks were banished to distant prefectures.

sentences.zh: 遷矩天官員外郎，竟為薛師所構，下獄，免官。

translations.literal: Ju was transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Celestial Offices; in the end he was framed by Master Xue, thrown into prison, and stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Ju was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Celestial Offices, but in the end Master Xue framed him; he was imprisoned and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 後有御醫沈南璆得幸，薛師恩漸衰，恨怒頗甚。

translations.literal: Later the imperial physician Shen Nanqiu won favor; Master Xue's favor gradually waned, and his resentment and wrath grew intense.
translations.idiomatic: Later the imperial physician Shen Nanqiu won the empress's favor; Master Xue's influence faded, and his resentment burned ever hotter.

sentences.zh: 證聖中，乃焚明堂、天堂，並為灰燼，則天愧而隱之，又令懷義充使督作。

translations.literal: During Zhengsheng, he burned the Bright Hall and Heavenly Hall to ashes; Zetian was ashamed and concealed it, again appointing Huaiyi as commissioner to supervise reconstruction.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhengsheng he set fire to the Bright Hall and Heavenly Hall and reduced them to ashes. Zetian was ashamed and hushed the matter up, then again appointed Huaiyi commissioner to supervise the rebuilding.

sentences.zh: 乃於明堂下置九州鼎，鑄銅為十二屬形象，置於本辰位，皆高一丈，懷義率人作號頭安置之。

translations.literal: Below the Bright Hall the Nine Provinces cauldrons were placed; bronze was cast into images of the Twelve Branches and set in their proper celestial positions, each one zhang high; Huaiyi led men as chant leaders to install them.
translations.idiomatic: Below the Bright Hall they placed the Nine Provinces cauldrons, cast bronze into images of the Twelve Branches, and set them in their proper celestial positions, each a full zhang in height; Huaiyi led the laborers as chant leaders to hoist them into place.

sentences.zh: 其後益驕倨，則天惡之，令太平公主擇膂力婦人數十，密防慮之。

translations.literal: Afterward he grew ever more arrogant; Zetian came to loathe him and had Princess Taiping select several dozen strong women to watch over him secretly.
translations.idiomatic: He grew ever more arrogant, and Zetian came to loathe him. She had Princess Taiping choose several dozen strong women to keep secret watch over him.

sentences.zh: 人有發其陰謀者，太平公主乳母張夫人令壯士縛而縊殺之，以輦車載屍送白馬寺。

translations.literal: When someone exposed his secret plots, Princess Taiping's wet nurse Lady Zhang had brawny men bind and strangle him, then sent his corpse by palanquin to White Horse Temple.
translations.idiomatic: When someone exposed his secret plots, Princess Taiping's wet nurse Lady Zhang had brawny men bind and strangle him, then sent his corpse by palanquin to White Horse Temple.

sentences.zh: 其侍者僧徒，皆流竄遠惡處。

translations.literal: His attendants and monk followers were all banished to remote, harsh regions.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants and monk followers were all banished to remote and harsh regions.

sentences.zh: =韋溫=

translations.literal: = Wei Wen =
translations.idiomatic: Wei Wen

sentences.zh: 韋溫，中宗韋庶人從父兄也。

translations.literal: Wei Wen was the paternal cousin of Emperor Zhongzong's Consort Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Wen was the paternal cousin of Emperor Zhongzong's Consort Wei.

sentences.zh: 父玄儼，高宗末官至許州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Xuanyan, in the final years of Gaozong's reign, reached the post of Prefect of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xuanyan, in the final years of Gaozong's reign, rose to Prefect of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 玄儼弟玄貞，初為普州參軍，以女為皇太子妃，擢拜豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Xuanyan's younger brother Xuanzhen, initially a military adjutant in Puzhou, was promoted to Prefect of Yuzhou when his daughter became the crown prince's consort.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanyan's younger brother Xuanzhen had begun as a military adjutant in Puzhou; when his daughter became the crown prince's consort, he was promoted to Prefect of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 中宗嗣位，妃為后。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong succeeded to the throne, the consort became empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong succeeded to the throne, the consort became empress.

sentences.zh: 及帝降為廬陵王，玄貞配流欽州而死。

translations.literal: When the emperor was demoted to Prince of Luling, Xuanzhen was sentenced to exile in Qinzhou and died there.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was demoted to Prince of Luling, Xuanzhen was exiled to Qinzhou and died there.

sentences.zh: 后母崔氏，為欽州首領寧承兄弟所殺。

translations.literal: The empress's mother, of the Cui clan, was killed by the brothers Ning Cheng, local chieftains of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's mother, Lady Cui, was killed by the brothers Ning Cheng, local chieftains of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 玄貞有四子：洵、浩、洞、泚，亦死於容州。

translations.literal: Xuanzhen had four sons—Xun, Hao, Dong, and Ci—who also died in Rongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzhen had four sons—Xun, Hao, Dong, and Ci—who also died in Rongzhou.

sentences.zh: 后二妹，逃竄獲免，間行歸長安。

translations.literal: The empress's two younger sisters fled and escaped with their lives, making their way back to Chang'an by secret routes.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's two younger sisters fled, escaped with their lives, and made their way back to Chang'an by secret routes.

sentences.zh: 及中宗復位，韋氏復為皇后。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong regained the throne, the Wei clan's daughter was again made empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong regained the throne, the Wei clan's daughter was again made empress.

sentences.zh: 其日，追贈玄貞為上洛郡王。

translations.literal: That same day, Xuanzhen was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Shangluo commandery.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Xuanzhen was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Shangluo.

sentences.zh: 左拾遺賈虛己上疏諫曰：「孔子曰：『惟名與器，不可以假人。

translations.literal: Left Reminder of Omissions Jia Xuji submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying: "Confucius said: 'Titles and instruments of office must not be lent to others.'
translations.idiomatic: Left Reminder of Omissions Jia Xuji submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying, "Confucius said, 'Titles and instruments of office must not be lent to others.'

sentences.zh: 』且非李氏而王，自古盟書所棄。

translations.literal: "Moreover, to enfeoff one not of the Li clan as king has been rejected in oaths since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: "Moreover, to enfeoff one not of the Li clan as king has been rejected in oaths since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 今陛下創制謀始，垂範將來，為皇王令圖，子孫明鏡。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is now founding institutions and laying plans that will set a model for future generations—a bright charter for kings and emperors, a mirror for your descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is now founding institutions and laying plans that will set a model for future generations—a bright charter for kings and emperors, a mirror for your descendants.

sentences.zh: 匡復未幾，后族有私，臣雖庸愚，尚知未可；

translations.literal: Not long after restoration, the empress's clan is already receiving private favors; though I am dull and ignorant, I still know this cannot be right;
translations.idiomatic: Not long after restoration, the empress's clan is already receiving private favors; though I am dull and ignorant, I still know this cannot be right;

sentences.zh: 史官執簡，必是直書。

translations.literal: The historiographers who hold the bamboo slips will surely record it truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographers who hold the bamboo slips will surely record it truthfully.

sentences.zh: 今萬姓颙然，聞一善令，莫不途歌里頌，延頸向風，欣然慕化，日恐不及。

translations.literal: The myriad people now look up with hope; hearing one good decree, none fail to sing it on the roads and praise it in their lanes, craning their necks toward the breeze, gladly yearning for reform, fearing each day that they will not receive enough.
translations.idiomatic: The myriad people now look up with hope; at one good decree they sing it on the roads and praise it in their lanes, craning their necks toward the breeze, gladly yearning for reform, fearing each day they will not receive enough.

sentences.zh: 陛下奈何行私惠，使樵夫議之。

translations.literal: How can Your Majesty grant private favors and let woodcutters discuss them?
translations.idiomatic: How can Your Majesty grant private favors and let woodcutters discuss them?

sentences.zh: 即先朝贈太原王，殷鑒不遠。

translations.literal: The recent precedent of enfeoffing the Prince of Taiyuan in the previous reign is a warning not far off.
translations.idiomatic: The recent precedent of enfeoffing the Prince of Taiyuan in the previous reign is a warning not far off.

sentences.zh: 同雲生於膚寸，尋木起於蘗栽，誠可惜也。

translations.literal: Clouds that bring rain rise from a finger's breadth; a towering tree springs from a stump—this would truly be a pity.
translations.idiomatic: Clouds that bring rain rise from a finger's breadth; a towering tree springs from a stump—this would truly be a pity.

sentences.zh: 渙汗既行，難改成命，臣望請皇后抗表固辭，使天下知弘讓之風，彤管著沖謙之德，是則巍巍聖鑒，無得而稱。

translations.literal: Since the decree has already been issued and is hard to revoke, I hope the empress may submit a memorial firmly declining it, so all under Heaven will know the spirit of magnanimous yielding, and the red brush will record her modest virtue—then Your Majesty's august judgment would be beyond praise.
translations.idiomatic: Since the decree has already been issued and is hard to revoke, I hope the empress may submit a memorial firmly declining it, so all under Heaven will know the spirit of magnanimous yielding, and the red brush will record her modest virtue—then Your Majesty's august judgment would be beyond praise.

sentences.zh: 」疏奏不省。

translations.literal: " The memorial was submitted but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but received no response.

sentences.zh: 尋又追贈玄貞為太師、雍州牧、益州大都督；

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Xuanzhen was again posthumously given the titles Grand Mentor, Governor of Yongzhou, and Great Protector-General of Yizhou;
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Xuanzhen was again posthumously given the titles Grand Mentor, Governor of Yongzhou, and Great Protector-General of Yizhou;

sentences.zh: 玄儼為特進、并州大都督、魯國公。

translations.literal: Xuanyan was made Special Advancement, Great Protector-General of Bingzhou, and Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanyan was made Special Advancement, Great Protector-General of Bingzhou, and Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 遣使迎玄貞及崔氏喪柩歸京師。

translations.literal: Envoys were sent to bring home the coffins of Xuanzhen and Lady Cui to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were sent to bring the coffins of Xuanzhen and Lady Cui home to the capital.

sentences.zh: 又遣廣州都督周仁軌率兵討斬寧承兄弟，以其首祭於崔氏。

translations.literal: Guangzhou Protector-General Zhou Rengui was also dispatched with troops to pursue and behead the brothers Ning Cheng, offering their heads in sacrifice before Lady Cui.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou Protector-General Zhou Rengui was also dispatched with troops to pursue and behead the brothers Ning Cheng, offering their heads in sacrifice before Lady Cui.

sentences.zh: 擢拜仁軌左羽林大將軍，賜爵汝南郡公，食實封五百戶。

translations.literal: Zhou Rengui was promoted to General of the Left Yulin Guard, granted the title Duke of Runan commandery, and given an actual fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Rengui was promoted to General of the Left Yulin Guard, enfeoffed as Duke of Runan, and granted an actual fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 及玄貞等柩將至，上與后登長樂宮，望喪而泣。

translations.literal: As the coffins of Xuanzhen and the others were about to arrive, the emperor and empress ascended Changle Palace, gazing toward the funeral procession and weeping.
translations.idiomatic: As the coffins of Xuanzhen and the others were about to arrive, the emperor and empress ascended Changle Palace, gazing toward the funeral procession and weeping.

sentences.zh: 加贈玄貞為酆王，謚曰文獻，仍號其廟曰褒德，陵曰榮先。

translations.literal: Xuanzhen received further posthumous honors as Prince of Feng, with posthumous title Wenxian; his temple was named Baoerde and his tomb Rongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzhen received further posthumous honors as Prince of Feng, with posthumous title Wenxian; his temple was named Baoerde and his tomb Rongxian.

sentences.zh: 各置官員，並給戶一百人守衛灑掃。

translations.literal: Officials were appointed for each, and one hundred households were assigned to guard and maintain them.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were appointed for each, and one hundred households were assigned to guard and maintain them.

sentences.zh: 又贈玄貞子洵為吏部尚書、汝南郡王，浩太常卿、武陵郡王，洞衛尉卿、淮南郡王，泚太僕卿、上蔡郡王，亦遣使迎其喪柩於京師。

translations.literal: Xuanzhen's sons were also posthumously honored: Xun as Minister of the Civil Service and Prince of Runan; Hao as Minister of Ceremonial and Prince of Wuling; Dong as Minister of the Guard and Prince of Huainan; Ci as Minister of the Stud and Prince of Shangcai—and envoys were sent to bring their coffins to the capital.
