translations.idiomatic: Xuanzhen's sons were also posthumously honored: Xun as Minister of the Civil Service and Prince of Runan; Hao as Minister of Ceremonial and Prince of Wuling; Dong as Minister of the Guard and Prince of Huainan; Ci as Minister of the Stud and Prince of Shangcai—and envoys were sent to bring their coffins to the capital.

sentences.zh: 溫，神龍中累遷禮部尚書，封魯國公。

translations.literal: During Shenlong, Wen was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Rites and enfeoffed Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: During Shenlong, Wen was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Rites and enfeoffed Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 弟湑，左羽林將軍，封曹國公。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xu was General of the Left Yulin Guard and Duke of Cao.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xu was General of the Left Yulin Guard and Duke of Cao.

sentences.zh: 后妹夫陸頌為國子祭酒，馮太和為太常少卿，太和尋卒，又適嗣虢王邕。

translations.literal: The empress's brother-in-law Lu Song was Director of the National University; Feng Taihe was Vice Minister of Ceremonial; Taihe soon died, and she remarried Heir of Prince Guo Yong.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's brother-in-law Lu Song was Director of the National University; Feng Taihe was Vice Minister of Ceremonies—Taihe soon died, and she remarried Heir of Prince Guo Yong.

sentences.zh: 湑子捷，尚成安公主，溫從祖弟濯，尚定安公主，皆拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Xu's son Jie married Princess Cheng'an; Wen's distant cousin Zhuo married Princess Ding'an; both were appointed Commandants of the Capital Garrisons of the Four Quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Xu's son Jie married Princess Cheng'an; Wen's distant cousin Zhuo married Princess Ding'an; both were appointed Imperial Son-in-Law Commandants.

sentences.zh: ，溫遷太子少保、同中書門下三品，仍遙授揚州大都督。

translations.literal: , Wen was promoted to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Co-signer of the Chancellery of the Three Departments, while also receiving the nominal appointment of Great Protector-General of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wen was promoted to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Co-signer of the Chancellery of the Three Departments, while also receiving the nominal appointment of Great Protector-General of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 溫等既居榮要，燻灼朝野，時人比之武氏。

translations.literal: Once Wen and his kin held exalted and critical posts, their splendor eclipsed court and realm; contemporaries compared them to the Wu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wen and his kin held exalted and critical posts, their splendor eclipsed court and realm; contemporaries compared them to the Wu clan.

sentences.zh: 湑及陸頌相次病卒，賻贈甚厚。

translations.literal: Xu and Lu Song died of illness in succession, and funeral gifts were lavish.
translations.idiomatic: Xu and Lu Song died of illness in succession, and funeral gifts were lavish.

sentences.zh: 及中宗崩，后令溫總知內外兵馬，守援宮掖。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong died, the empress ordered Wen to take overall command of inner and outer military forces and guard the palace precincts.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong died, the empress ordered Wen to take overall command of inner and outer military forces and guard the palace precincts.

sentences.zh: 又引從子播、族弟璇、弟捷、濯等，分掌屯營及左右羽林軍。

translations.literal: She also brought in her nephew Bo, clan cousin Xuan, younger brother Jie, Zhuo, and others to divide command of encampment garrisons and the Left and Right Yulin Armies.
translations.idiomatic: She also brought in her nephew Bo, clan cousin Xuan, younger brother Jie, Zhuo, and others to divide command of encampment garrisons and the Left and Right Yulin Armies.

sentences.zh: 臨淄王討韋氏，溫等皆坐斬，宗族無少長皆死，語在《韋庶人傳》。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Linzi suppressed the Wei clan, Wen and the rest were all executed by decapitation; none of the clan, young or old, survived—the account is given in the Biography of Consort Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Linzi suppressed the Wei clan, Wen and the rest were all executed; none of the clan, young or old, survived—the account is given in the Biography of Consort Wei.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，仍令削平玄貞及洵等墳墓。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, he ordered the tombs of Xuanzhen, Xun, and the others leveled.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong took the throne, he ordered the tombs of Xuanzhen, Xun, and the others leveled.

sentences.zh: =王仁皎　=

translations.literal: = Wang Renjiao =
translations.idiomatic: Wang Renjiao

sentences.zh: 王仁皎，玄宗王庶人父也。

translations.literal: Wang Renjiao was the father of Emperor Xuanzong's Consort Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Renjiao was the father of Emperor Xuanzong's Consort Wang.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，官至長上果毅。

translations.literal: During Jinglong he reached the rank of Senior Commander of the Changshang Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During Jinglong he reached the rank of Senior Commander of the Changshang Guard.

sentences.zh: 玄宗即位，以后父，歷將作大匠、太僕卿，遷開府儀同三司，封祁國公。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong ascended the throne, as the empress's father he served successively as Director of Imperial Construction and Minister of the Stud, then was made Honorary Grand Master with the status of the Three Highest Offices and enfeoffed Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong ascended the throne, as the empress's father he served successively as Director of Imperial Construction and Minister of the Stud, then was made Honorary Grand Master with the status of the Three Highest Offices and enfeoffed Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 仁皎不預朝政，但厚自奉養，積子女財貨而已。

translations.literal: Renjiao took no part in governance but lived in lavish self-indulgence, amassing wealth for his sons and daughters—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Renjiao took no part in governance but lived in lavish self-indulgence, amassing wealth for his sons and daughters—that was all.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太尉，官供葬事。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously appointed Grand Commandant; the state provided his funeral.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed Grand Commandant; the state provided his funeral.

sentences.zh: 柩車既發，上於望春亭遙望之，令張說為其碑文，玄宗親書石焉。

translations.literal: When the funeral procession set out, the emperor watched from afar at Wangchun Pavilion, had Zhang Yue compose his epitaph, and Xuanzong personally inscribed the stone.
translations.idiomatic: When the funeral procession set out, the emperor watched from afar at Wangchun Pavilion, had Zhang Yue compose his epitaph, and Xuanzong personally inscribed the stone.

sentences.zh: 子守一。

translations.literal: Son: Shouyi.
translations.idiomatic: Son: Shouyi.

sentences.zh: 守一與后雙生。

translations.literal: Shouyi and the empress were twins.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyi and the empress were twins.

sentences.zh: 守一與玄宗有舊，及上登極，以清陽公主妻之。

translations.literal: Shouyi had long standing with Xuanzong; when the emperor took the throne, he gave him Princess Qingyang in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyi had long standing with Xuanzong; when the emperor took the throne, he gave him Princess Qingyang in marriage.

sentences.zh: 從討蕭至忠、岑羲等有功，自尚乘奉御遷殿中少監，特封晉國公，累轉太子少保。

translations.literal: For merit in the campaign against Xiao Zhizhong, Cen Xi, and others, he rose from Chief Groom of the Imperial Carriage to Vice Director of the Palace Administration, was specially enfeoffed Duke of Jin, and was eventually promoted to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: For merit in the campaign against Xiao Zhizhong, Cen Xi, and others, he rose from Chief Groom of the Imperial Carriage to Vice Director of the Palace Administration, was specially enfeoffed Duke of Jin, and was eventually promoted to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 父卒，襲爵祁國公。

translations.literal: When his father died, he inherited the title Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he inherited the title Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 十一年，坐與庶人潛通左道，左遷柳州司馬，行至藍田驛，賜死。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, for secretly practicing heterodox arts with the deposed consort, he was demoted to Military Assistant of Liuzhou; on reaching Lantian post station he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, for secretly practicing heterodox arts with the deposed consort, he was demoted to Military Assistant of Liuzhou; on reaching Lantian post station he was granted death.

sentences.zh: 守一性貪鄙，積財巨萬，及籍沒其家，財帛不可勝計。

translations.literal: Shouyi was greedy and base by nature and amassed wealth in the tens of thousands; when his household was confiscated, goods and cash beyond reckoning were found.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyi was greedy and base by nature and amassed wealth in the tens of thousands; when his household was confiscated, goods and cash beyond reckoning were found.

sentences.zh: =吳溆　=

translations.literal: = Wu Xu =
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xu

sentences.zh: 吳溆，章敬皇后之弟也，濮州濮陽人。

translations.literal: Wu Xu was the younger brother of Empress Zhangjing, a native of Puyang in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xu was the younger brother of Empress Zhangjing, a native of Puyang in Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖神泉，位終縣令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shenquan ended his career as county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shenquan ended his career as county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 父令珪，益州郫縣丞。

translations.literal: His father Lingui was assistant magistrate of Pi County in Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lingui was assistant magistrate of Pi County in Yizhou.

sentences.zh: ，代宗始封拜外族，贈神泉司徒，令珪太尉，令珪母弟前宣城令令瑤為開府儀同三司、太子家令，封濮陽郡公；

translations.literal: , when Daizong first began enfeoffing maternal kin, Shenquan was posthumously made Director of the Masses, Lingui Grand Commandant, and Lingui's younger maternal half-brother the former magistrate of Xuancheng Lingyao was made Honorary Grand Master with the status of the Three Highest Offices and Director of the Heir Apparent's Household, enfeoffed Duke of Puyang commandery;
translations.idiomatic: When Daizong first began enfeoffing maternal kin, Shenquan was posthumously made Director of the Masses, Lingui Grand Commandant, and Lingui's younger maternal half-brother the former magistrate of Xuancheng Lingyao was made Honorary Grand Master with the status of the Three Highest Offices and Director of the Heir Apparent's Household, enfeoffed Duke of Puyang;

sentences.zh: 中郎將令瑜為開府儀同三司、太子諭德、濟陽郡公。

translations.literal: Middle General Lingyu was made Honorary Grand Master with the status of the Three Highest Offices, Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and Duke of Jiyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Middle General Lingyu was made Honorary Grand Master with the status of the Three Highest Offices, Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and Duke of Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 漵時為盛王府錄事參軍，拜開府儀同三司、太子詹事、濮陽郡公。

translations.literal: At the time Xu was Recording Officer of the Shengwang mansion; he was appointed Honorary Grand Master with the status of the Three Highest Offices, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and Duke of Puyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xu was Recording Officer of the Shengwang mansion; he was appointed Honorary Grand Master with the status of the Three Highest Offices, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and Duke of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 以元舅遷鴻臚少卿、金吾將軍。

translations.literal: As chief maternal uncle he was transferred to Vice Minister of State Ceremonials and General of the Gold Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: As chief maternal uncle he was transferred to Vice Minister of State Ceremonials and General of the Gold Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 建中初，遷大將軍。

translations.literal: At the start of Jianzhong he was promoted to Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jianzhong he was promoted to Grand General.

sentences.zh: 漵雖居戚屬，恭遜謙和，人皆重之。

translations.literal: Though Xu held imperial kinship, he was deferential, modest, and courteous, and all held him in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xu held imperial kinship, he was deferential, modest, and courteous, and all held him in esteem.

sentences.zh: 涇師之亂，從幸奉天，盧杞、白志貞謂德宗曰：「臣細觀硃泚心跡，必不至為戎首，佇當效順。

translations.literal: During the Jingyuan mutiny, he accompanied the emperor to Fengtian. Lu Qi and Bai Zhizhen said to Dezong: "We have closely observed Zhu Ci's intentions; he will surely not take the lead in rebellion and will soon submit."
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingyuan mutiny, he accompanied the emperor to Fengtian. Lu Qi and Bai Zhizhen said to Dezong, "We have closely observed Zhu Ci's intentions; he will surely not take the lead in rebellion and will soon submit."

sentences.zh: 宜擇大臣一人，入京師慰諭，以觀其心。

translations.literal: Choose one chief minister to enter the capital and reassure him, to test his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Choose one chief minister to enter the capital and reassure him, to test his heart.

sentences.zh: 」上召從幸群臣言之，皆憚其行。

translations.literal: " The emperor summoned the officials who had accompanied him and put the matter before them; all feared to go.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned the officials who had accompanied him and put the matter before them; all feared to go.

sentences.zh: 漵起奏曰：「不以臣才望無堪，臣願北行。

translations.literal: Xu rose and memorialized: "Do not mind that I lack talent and standing—I am willing to go north.
translations.idiomatic: Xu rose and memorialized, "Do not mind that I lack talent and standing—I am willing to go north.

sentences.zh: 」德宗甚悅。

translations.literal: " Dezong was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 漵退而謂人曰：「人臣食君之祿，死君之難，臨危自計，非忠也。

translations.literal: Xu withdrew and said to others: "A minister who eats his lord's stipend ought to die in his lord's peril; to calculate one's own safety at a crisis is not loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Xu withdrew and said to others, "A minister who eats his lord's stipend ought to die in his lord's peril; to calculate one's own safety at a crisis is not loyalty.

sentences.zh: 吾忝戚屬，今日委身於賊，誠知必死，不欲聖情慊於無人犯難也。

translations.literal: I bear the shame of imperial kinship; today I throw myself into the rebel's hands. I know I shall surely die, but I do not wish the sacred heart to be vexed that no one would brave the peril.
translations.idiomatic: I bear the shame of imperial kinship; today I throw myself into the rebel's hands. I know I shall surely die, but I do not wish the sacred heart to be vexed that no one would brave the peril.

sentences.zh: 」即日賫詔見泚，深陳上待屬之意。

translations.literal: " That same day he carried the edict to see Zhu Ci and spoke at length of the emperor's regard for the imperial kin.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he carried the edict to see Zhu Ci and spoke at length of the emperor's regard for the imperial kin.

sentences.zh: 時泚逆謀已定，貌雖從命，而心已異，乃留漵於客省，竟被害。

translations.literal: By then Zhu Ci's treacherous designs were fixed; though he outwardly obeyed, inwardly his heart had already turned, and he detained Xu in the guest hall, where Xu was ultimately killed.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhu Ci's treacherous designs were fixed; though he outwardly obeyed, inwardly his heart had already turned, and he detained Xu in the guest hall, where Xu was ultimately killed.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，悲悼不已，贈太子太傅，賜其家實封二百戶，一子五品正員官，敕收城日葬事官給。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he mourned without end, posthumously appointing Xu Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, granting his family an actual fief of two hundred households, one son a regular fifth-rank office, and ordering that when the capital was recovered the state would provide the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it, he mourned without end, posthumously appointing Xu Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, granting his family an actual fief of two hundred households, one son a regular fifth-rank office, and ordering that when the capital was recovered the state would provide the funeral.

sentences.zh: 弟湊。

translations.literal: Younger brother: Cou.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother: Cou.

sentences.zh: 湊，寶歷中與兄漵同日開府，授太子詹事，俱封濮陽郡公。

translations.literal: Cou, in Baoli, on the same day as his elder brother Xu received the opening of an honorary mansion and was appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent; both were enfeoffed Duke of Puyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Cou, in Baoli, on the same day as his elder brother Xu received the opening of an honorary mansion and was appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent; both were enfeoffed Duke of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 湊以兄弟三品，固辭太過，乞授卑官。

translations.literal: Cou, considering it excessive that both brothers held third rank, firmly declined and requested a lesser appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Cou, considering it excessive that both brothers held third rank, firmly declined and requested a lesser appointment.

sentences.zh: 乃以湊檢校太子賓客，兼太子家令，充十宅王使。

translations.literal: He was then made Acting Counselor to the Heir Apparent, concurrently Director of the Heir Apparent's Household, and Commissioner for the Ten Princely Residences.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Acting Counselor to the Heir Apparent, concurrently Director of the Heir Apparent's Household, and Commissioner for the Ten Princely Residences.

sentences.zh: 累轉左金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He was successively transferred to Grand General of the Left Jinwu Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively transferred to Grand General of the Left Jinwu Guard.

sentences.zh: 湊小心謹慎，智識周敏，特承顧問，偏見委信。

translations.literal: Cou was cautious and prudent, quick and thorough in judgment, and received special consultation and partial trust.
translations.idiomatic: Cou was cautious and prudent, quick and thorough in judgment, and received special consultation and partial trust.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，滑帥令狐彰、汴帥田神功相次歿於理所，時籓方兵驕，乘戎帥喪亡，人情多梗。

translations.literal: During Dali, Hu Lingzhang, military commissioner of Hua, and Tian Shen'gong, military commissioner of Bian, died in succession at their posts; at the time frontier armies were arrogant, and with the commanders' deaths popular sentiment grew restless in many places.
translations.idiomatic: During Dali, Hu Lingzhang, military commissioner of Hua, and Tian Shen'gong, military commissioner of Bian, died in succession at their posts; frontier armies were arrogant, and with the commanders' deaths popular sentiment grew restless in many places.

sentences.zh: 代宗命湊銜命撫慰，至必委曲說諭，隨所欲為之奏請，皆得軍民和協，帝深重之。

translations.literal: Daizong ordered Cou to go on imperial commission to reassure them; wherever he arrived he tactfully persuaded and memorialized for whatever they desired, achieving harmony between armies and people; the emperor valued him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong ordered Cou to go on imperial commission to reassure them; wherever he arrived he tactfully persuaded and memorialized for whatever they desired, achieving harmony between armies and people; the emperor valued him deeply.

sentences.zh: 宰臣元載弄權，招致賄賂，醜跡日彰。

translations.literal: Chancellor Yuan Zai manipulated power, solicited bribes, and his shameful conduct grew more conspicuous day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Yuan Zai manipulated power, solicited bribes, and his shameful conduct grew more conspicuous day by day.

sentences.zh: 帝惡之，將加之法，恐左右泄漏，無與言者，唯與湊密計圖之。

translations.literal: The emperor hated him and intended to punish him by law, but feared leaks among those close at hand and had no one to speak with—he confided only in Cou to plan it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hated him and intended to punish him by law, but feared leaks among those close at hand and had no one to speak with—he confided only in Cou to plan it.

sentences.zh: 及收載於內侍省，同列王縉，其黨楊炎、王昂、韓洄、包佶、韓會等，皆當從坐籍沒。

translations.literal: When Zai was arrested in the Inner Palace Service, his colleague Wang Jin and his partisans Yang Yan, Wang Ang, Han Hui, Bao Ji, Han Hui, and others were all subject to guilt by association and confiscation.
translations.idiomatic: When Zai was arrested in the Inner Palace Service, his colleague Wang Jin and his partisans Yang Yan, Wang Ang, Han Hui, Bao Ji, Han Hui, and others were all subject to guilt by association and confiscation.

sentences.zh: 湊諫救百端，言「法宜從寬，縉等從坐，理不至死。

translations.literal: Cou remonstrated at length in their defense, saying, "The law should be applied with lenience; Wang Jin and the others, guilty by association, do not deserve death in principle.
translations.idiomatic: Cou remonstrated at length in their defense, saying, "The law should be applied with lenience; Wang Jin and the others, guilty by association, do not deserve death in principle.

sentences.zh: 若不降以等差，一例極刑，恐虧損聖德。

translations.literal: If distinctions in punishment are not granted and all receive the extreme penalty alike, I fear the sacred virtue will be diminished.
translations.idiomatic: If distinctions in punishment are not granted and all receive the extreme penalty alike, I fear the sacred virtue will be diminished.

sentences.zh: 」由是縉等得減死，流貶之。

translations.literal: " Thereby Wang Jin and the rest had their death sentences commuted and were banished.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby Wang Jin and the rest had their death sentences commuted and were banished.

sentences.zh: 大歷末，丁繼母喪免。

translations.literal: At the end of Dali he was dismissed to observe mourning for his stepmother.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Dali he was dismissed to observe mourning for his stepmother.

sentences.zh: 建中初，起為右衛將軍，兼通州刺史。

translations.literal: At the start of Jianzhong he was recalled as General of the Right Guard, concurrently Prefect of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jianzhong he was recalled as General of the Right Guard, concurrently Prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，入為太子賓客，出為福州刺史、御史中丞、福建觀察使。

translations.literal: At the start of Zhenyuan he entered court as Counselor to the Heir Apparent, then went out as Prefect of Fuzhou, Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Military Commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Zhenyuan he entered court as Counselor to the Heir Apparent, then went out as Prefect of Fuzhou, Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Military Commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 為政勤儉清苦，美譽日聞。

translations.literal: In governing he was diligent, frugal, and austere, and his good reputation spread day by day.
translations.idiomatic: In governing he was diligent, frugal, and austere, and his good reputation spread day by day.

sentences.zh: 宰相竇參以私怨惡之，數加譖毀，又言湊風病，不任趨馳。

translations.literal: Chancellor Dou Can hated him for a private grudge and repeatedly slandered and defamed him, also saying that Cou suffered from wind illness and was unfit for rushing about on official business.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Dou Can bore him a private grudge and repeatedly slandered him, claiming moreover that Cou suffered a paralytic affliction and could not keep up with the duties that required him to hurry to and fro.

sentences.zh: 德宗召湊至京師，對於別殿，上令殿上行走，以驗其病否，由是悟參之誣，因是惡參。

translations.literal: Dezong summoned Cou to the capital and received him in a separate hall; the emperor ordered him to walk about the hall to test whether he was ill, and thereby realized Can's false accusation and came to hate Can.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong summoned Cou to the capital and received him in a side hall, ordering him to walk back and forth across the hall to test whether he was truly ill. Thereby the emperor saw through Can's false accusation and turned against him.

sentences.zh: 尋以湊為陜州大都督府長史、陜虢觀察使，以代參之黨李翼。

translations.literal: Soon Cou was appointed Chief Administrator of the Shanzhou Superior Prefecture, Military Commissioner of Shan-Guo, replacing Li Yi, a partisan of Can.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Cou was made Chief Administrator of the Shanzhou Superior Prefecture and Military Commissioner of Shan-Guo, replacing Li Yi, a partisan of Can.

sentences.zh: 會劉玄佐卒，以湊檢校兵部尚書、汴州刺史、御史大夫、宣武軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Liu Xuanzuo died, Cou was made Acting Minister of War, Prefect of Bianzhou, Censor-in-Chief, and Military Commissioner of the Xuanwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Xuanzuo died, Cou was appointed Acting Minister of War, Prefect of Bianzhou, Censor-in-Chief, and Military Commissioner of the Xuanwu Army.

sentences.zh: 時汴州軍亂，殺牙將曹金岸、縣令李邁，謀立玄佐子士寧。

translations.literal: At the time the Bianzhou army was in revolt; they killed the yabing general Cao Jin'an and the magistrate Li Mai and plotted to install Xuanzuo's son Shining.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Bianzhou army was in revolt. The mutineers killed the yabing general Cao Jin'an and the magistrate Li Mai and plotted to install Xuanzuo's son Shining as commander.

sentences.zh: 上將遣兵送湊赴鎮，召宰臣議。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to dispatch troops to escort Cou to his post and summoned the chief ministers to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to dispatch troops to escort Cou to his post and summoned the chief ministers to counsel him.

sentences.zh: 竇參深沮其行，恐軍中拒命，乃召湊回，授右金吾衛大將軍，而以梁宋節鉞授士寧。

translations.literal: Dou Can strongly obstructed the journey, fearing the army would refuse orders; he then recalled Cou and appointed him Grand General of the Right Jinwu Guard, while granting the military commission of Liang and Song to Shining.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Can strongly opposed the move, fearing the army would refuse to obey. He had Cou recalled and appointed Grand General of the Right Jinwu Guard, while the military commission over Liang and Song was given to Shining instead.

sentences.zh: 春夏旱，穀貴，人多流亡。

translations.literal: In spring and summer there was drought; grain was costly, and many people fled as refugees.
translations.idiomatic: Drought struck in spring and summer; grain prices soared, and many people fled their homes.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹韓臯以政事不理黜官。

translations.literal: Han Gao, Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, was dismissed from office for failing to govern affairs properly.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gao, Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, was dismissed for mismanaging the administration.

sentences.zh: 上召湊，面授京兆尹，即日令視事，經宿方下制。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Cou and personally appointed him Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao; that same day he was ordered to assume duties, and only after one night was the formal edict issued.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Cou and personally appointed him Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao. That same day Cou was ordered to take up his duties; the formal edict was not issued until the following day.

sentences.zh: 湊孜孜為理，以勤儉為務，人樂其政。

translations.literal: Cou was assiduous in governing and made diligence and frugality his task; the people rejoiced in his administration.
translations.idiomatic: Cou governed with tireless diligence and made thrift his watchword; the people welcomed his rule.

sentences.zh: 時宮中選內官買物於市，倚勢強買物，不充價，人畏而避之，呼為「宮市」。

translations.literal: At the time the palace selected inner officials to buy goods in the market; relying on their power they forcibly purchased goods without paying full price, and people feared them and avoided them, calling this the "Palace Market."
translations.idiomatic: At the time the palace sent eunuchs into the markets to buy goods. Leaning on their authority, they forced purchases and paid less than fair price. People feared them and kept out of their way, calling the practice the "Palace Market."

sentences.zh: 掌賦者多與中貴人交結假借，不言其弊。

translations.literal: Most revenue officials cultivated ties with eminent eunuchs and borrowed their influence, and did not speak of the abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Most revenue officials cultivated ties with powerful eunuchs and borrowed their influence, and none spoke of the abuse.

sentences.zh: 湊為京尹，便殿從容論之，曰：「物議以中人買物於市，稍不便於人，此事甚細，虛掇流議。

translations.literal: As Metropolitan Governor, Cou discussed the matter at leisure in the informal hall, saying, "Public opinion holds that eunuchs buying goods in the market is somewhat inconvenient for the people. The matter is very minor and needlessly stirs loose talk.
translations.idiomatic: As metropolitan governor, Cou raised the matter at leisure in the informal hall, saying, "Public opinion holds that eunuchs buying goods in the market is somewhat inconvenient for the people. The matter is very minor and needlessly stirs loose talk.

sentences.zh: 凡宮中所須，責臣可辦，不必更差中使。

translations.literal: Whatever the palace requires, charge your subject to supply it; there is no need to dispatch eunuch envoys again.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever the palace requires, your subject can supply it; there is no need to send eunuch envoys again.

sentences.zh: 若以臣府縣外吏，不合預聞宮中所須，則乞選內官年高謹重者，充宮市令，庶息人間論議。

translations.literal: If, as a prefectural and county official outside the palace, your subject is not fit to be informed of the palace's needs, then I beg that older, grave inner officials be chosen to serve as Palace Market commissioners, so that public discussion may be stilled.
translations.idiomatic: If, as a prefectural official outside the palace, I am not fit to be told what the palace needs, then I beg that older, sober eunuchs be chosen to serve as Palace Market commissioners, so that public complaint may cease.

sentences.zh: 」又奏：「掌閑彍騎、飛龍內園、芙蓉及禁軍諸司等使，雜供手力資課太多，量宜減省。

translations.literal: " He also memorialized: "The commissioners of the Palace Leisure Archery Cavalry, the Inner Garden Flying Dragon Office, the Hibiscus Office, and the various offices of the Palace Army levy too many miscellaneous labor-service fees and contributions; these should be reduced as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: " He also memorialized: "The commissioners of the Palace Leisure Archery Cavalry, the Inner Garden Flying Dragon Office, the Hibiscus Office, and the various offices of the Palace Army levy too many miscellaneous labor-service fees and contributions; these should be reduced as appropriate.

sentences.zh: 」上多從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor largely followed his recommendations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor largely followed his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 初，府掾吏以湊起自戚籓，不諳簿領，凡有疑獄難決之事，多候湊將出時方呈，冀免指擿瑕病。

translations.literal: At first the prefectural clerks, because Cou had risen from imperial kin in a frontier post and was unfamiliar with ledgers and documents, whenever there were doubtful cases hard to decide would mostly wait until Cou was about to leave before presenting them, hoping to escape having flaws pointed out.
translations.idiomatic: At first the prefectural clerks, thinking Cou had risen from imperial kin in a frontier post and was unfamiliar with ledgers and documents, would wait until he was about to leave before presenting doubtful cases that were hard to decide, hoping to escape having their errors exposed.

sentences.zh: 湊雖倉卒閱視，必指其奸幸之處，下筆決斷，無毫厘之差。

translations.literal: Though Cou reviewed them in haste, he always pointed out where fraud and favoritism lay, put pen to paper and decided, without the slightest error.
translations.idiomatic: Even when he reviewed them in haste, Cou always pinpointed where fraud and favoritism lay, wrote his decision, and never missed by the slightest margin.

sentences.zh: 掾吏非大過，不行笞責；

translations.literal: For clerks who had not committed grave offenses he did not impose flogging and punishment;
translations.idiomatic: For clerks who had not committed grave offenses he did not impose flogging;

sentences.zh: 而召面按問，詰責而釋之。

translations.literal: instead he summoned them for face-to-face inquiry, questioned and rebuked them, and then released them.
translations.idiomatic: instead he summoned them for face-to-face questioning, rebuked them, and let them go.

sentences.zh: 吏尤惕厲，庶務咸舉。

translations.literal: The clerks became especially vigilant and cautious, and all routine affairs were properly handled.
translations.idiomatic: The clerks became especially vigilant, and all routine affairs were properly handled.

sentences.zh: 文敬太子、義章公主相繼薨歿，上深追念，葬送之儀頗厚。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Wenjing and Princess Yizhang died in succession; the emperor mourned them deeply, and the rites of burial and send-off were quite lavish.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Wenjing and Princess Yizhang died in succession. The emperor mourned them deeply, and the rites of burial and send-off were quite lavish.

sentences.zh: 召集工役，載土築墳，妨民農務。

translations.literal: Laborers were summoned, earth was hauled to build tombs, and the people's farm work was obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: Laborers were summoned to haul earth and build tombs, disrupting the people's farm work.

sentences.zh: 湊候上顧問，極言之。

translations.literal: Cou waited for the emperor to turn to him for counsel and spoke out fully.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor turned to him for counsel, Cou spoke out fully.

sentences.zh: 宗屬門吏以湊論諫太繁，恐上厭苦，每以簡約規之。

translations.literal: The gate officials of the imperial kin, because Cou's remonstrances were too frequent, feared the emperor would grow weary and vexed, and often admonished him to be brief.
translations.idiomatic: The gate officials of the imperial kin, fearing that Cou's remonstrances were too frequent and would weary the emperor, often urged him to be brief.

sentences.zh: 湊曰：「聖上明哲，憂勞四海，必不以公主、太子之鐘念而忽疲民。

translations.literal: Cou said, "The sage sovereign is clear-sighted and toils for all under Heaven; he surely will not, because of lingering grief for the princess and crown prince, heedlessly exhaust the people.
translations.idiomatic: Cou said, "The sage sovereign is clear-sighted and toils for all under Heaven. He surely will not, out of lingering grief for the princess and crown prince, heedlessly exhaust the people.

sentences.zh: 但人多順旨不言，若再三啟諫，必動宸情，則生民受賜。

translations.literal: But many people simply agree with the sovereign's wishes and do not speak; if one remonstrates again and again, the imperial heart will surely be moved, and then the common people will receive the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: But many people simply agree with the sovereign's wishes and say nothing. If one remonstrates again and again, the imperial heart will surely be moved, and the common people will receive the benefit.

sentences.zh: 長吏不言，是為阿旨。

translations.literal: For a chief official not to speak is to curry favor with the sovereign's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: For a chief official not to speak is to curry favor with the sovereign's wishes.

sentences.zh: 如窮民上訴，罪在何人？

translations.literal: If the poor people appeal in complaint, upon whom will the guilt fall?
translations.idiomatic: If the poor people appeal in complaint, upon whom will the guilt fall?

sentences.zh: 」議者重之。

translations.literal: " Commentators respected this.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators respected this.

sentences.zh: 以能政，兼兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Because of his capable administration, he was additionally appointed Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his capable administration, he was additionally appointed Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 官街樹缺，所司植榆以補之，湊曰：「榆非九衢之玩。

translations.literal: Where trees were missing on the official avenues, the responsible offices planted elms to fill the gaps; Cou said, "Elms are not ornament for the nine thoroughfares.
translations.idiomatic: Where trees were missing on the official avenues, the responsible offices planted elms to fill the gaps. Cou said, "Elms are not fit ornament for the capital's main thoroughfares.

sentences.zh: 」亟命易之以槐。

translations.literal: " He immediately ordered them replaced with pagoda trees.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered them replaced with pagoda trees.

sentences.zh: 及槐陰成而湊卒，人指樹而懷之。

translations.literal: By the time the pagoda trees cast shade, Cou had died; people pointed to the trees and cherished his memory.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the pagoda trees cast shade, Cou had died; people pointed to the trees and cherished his memory.

sentences.zh: 湊於德宗為老舅，漢魏故事，多退居散地，才免罪戾而已。

translations.literal: Cou was Dezong's elder maternal uncle; by Han and Wei precedent, such kin mostly retired to honorific posts and barely escaped guilt and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Cou was Dezong's elder maternal uncle. By Han and Wei precedent, such kin mostly retired to honorific posts and barely escaped guilt and punishment.

sentences.zh: 湊自貞元已來，特承恩顧，歷中外顯貴，雖聖獎隆深，亦由湊小心辦事，奉職有方故也。

translations.literal: From Zhenyuan onward Cou received special imperial favor and passed through prominent posts at court and in the provinces; though the sage's commendation was deep and generous, it was also because Cou was careful in handling affairs and performed his duties with method.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhenyuan onward Cou received special imperial favor and held prominent posts at court and in the provinces. Though the emperor's commendation was deep and generous, it was also because Cou was careful in handling affairs and performed his duties with method.

sentences.zh: 湊既疾，不召巫醫，藥不入口，家人泣而勉之。

translations.literal: Once Cou fell ill, he did not summon shamans or physicians; medicine did not pass his lips, and his family wept as they urged him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Cou fell ill, he would summon neither shamans nor physicians. Medicine did not pass his lips, and his family wept as they urged him to take it.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「吾以凡才，濫因外戚進用，起家便授三品，歷顯位四十年，壽登七十，為人足矣，更欲何求？

translations.literal: He replied, "With my ordinary talent I was improperly promoted through imperial kinship; from the start of my career I was granted third rank, held prominent posts for forty years, and have reached seventy years of life — as a man I have had enough; what more could I seek?
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "With my ordinary talent I was improperly promoted through imperial kinship. From the start of my career I was granted third rank, held prominent posts for forty years, and have reached seventy years of life — as a man I have had enough. What more could I seek?

sentences.zh: 古之以親戚進用者，罕有善終，吾得歸全以侍先人，幸也。

translations.literal: Of those promoted through kinship in antiquity, few ended well; that I may die whole and attend my forebears is good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Of those promoted through kinship in antiquity, few ended well. That I may die whole and attend my forebears is good fortune.

sentences.zh: 」德宗知之，令御醫進藥，不獲已，服之。

translations.literal: " When Dezong learned of this, he ordered the imperial physician to present medicine; unable to refuse, Cou took it.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong learned of this, he ordered the imperial physician to present medicine. Unable to refuse, Cou took it.

sentences.zh: 四月卒，時年七十一，贈尚書左僕射，罷朝一日。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he died, at the age of seventy-one; he was posthumously appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and court was suspended for one day.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth month at the age of seventy-one. He was posthumously appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and court was suspended for one day.

sentences.zh: =竇覦=

translations.literal: = Dou Di =
translations.idiomatic: Dou Di

sentences.zh: 竇覦，昭成皇后族侄。

translations.literal: Dou Di was a clansman nephew of Empress Zhaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Di was a clansman nephew of Empress Zhaocheng.

sentences.zh: 父光，華原尉。

translations.literal: His father Guang was Assistant Magistrate of Huayuan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guang was Assistant Magistrate of Huayuan.

sentences.zh: 覦以親廕，釋褐右衛率府兵曹參軍。

translations.literal: Di entered service through kinship privilege and upon first appointment became Army Staff Officer of the Right Guard Commandant's Office.
translations.idiomatic: Di entered service through kinship privilege and upon first appointment became Army Staff Officer of the Right Guard Commandant's Office.

sentences.zh: 鄜坊節度臧希讓奏為判官，累授監察殿中侍御史、檢校工部員外郎、坊州刺史。

translations.literal: Zang Xirang, military commissioner of Fufang, memorialized to appoint him judge; he was successively appointed Supervising Censor, Palace Censor, Acting Vice Minister of Works, and Prefect of Fangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Xirang, military commissioner of Fufang, memorialized to appoint him judge. He was successively appointed Supervising Censor, Palace Censor, Acting Vice Minister of Works, and Prefect of Fangzhou.

sentences.zh: ，討李懷光於河中，詔覦以坊州兵七百人屯邰陽。

translations.literal: , when campaigning against Li Huaiguang at Hezhong, an edict ordered Di to garrison seven hundred Fangzhou troops at Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: When campaigning against Li Huaiguang at Hezhong, an edict ordered Di to garrison seven hundred Fangzhou troops at Heyang.

sentences.zh: 賊平，以功兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, for his merit he was additionally appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were pacified, he was additionally appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief for his merit.

sentences.zh: 遷同州刺史，入朝為戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Prefect of Tongzhou, then entered court as Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Prefect of Tongzhou, then entered court as Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 覦無他才伎，為吏有計數，又以韓滉子婿，故籓府辟召，遂歷牧守。

translations.literal: Di had no other talent or skill, but as an official he was shrewd in calculation; moreover, as son-in-law of Han Huang, he was recruited by frontier headquarters and thus passed through governorships.
translations.idiomatic: Di had no other talent or skill, but as an official he was shrewd in calculation. Moreover, as son-in-law of Han Huang, he was recruited by frontier headquarters and thus rose through governorships.

sentences.zh: 宰相竇參，覦再從侄。

translations.literal: Chancellor Dou Can was Di's second cousin once removed.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Dou Can was Di's second cousin once removed.

sentences.zh: 參少依覦，及參秉政，力薦於朝，故有貳卿之拜。

translations.literal: Can in youth relied on Di, and once Can held power he vigorously recommended him at court; hence the appointment to a vice-ministerial post.
translations.idiomatic: Can in youth had relied on Di, and once Can held power he vigorously recommended him at court; hence the appointment to a vice-ministerial post.

sentences.zh: 數月，為揚州大都督府長史、御史大夫、充淮南節度副大使、知節度事，既非德舉，人咸薄之。

translations.literal: Within a few months he was made Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou Superior Prefecture, Censor-in-Chief, Deputy Military Commissioner of Huainan, and Acting Military Commissioner; since this was not a promotion based on virtue, all looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months he was made Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou Superior Prefecture, Censor-in-Chief, Deputy Military Commissioner of Huainan, and Acting Military Commissioner. Since this was not a promotion based on merit, all looked down on him.

sentences.zh: 赴鎮旬日，暴卒，詔贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Within ten days of reaching his post he died suddenly; an edict posthumously appointed him Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days of reaching his post he died suddenly. An edict posthumously appointed him Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: =柳晟=

translations.literal: = Liu Sheng =
translations.idiomatic: Liu Sheng

sentences.zh: 柳晟者，肅宗皇后之甥。

translations.literal: Liu Sheng was a nephew of Suzong's empress.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Sheng was a nephew of Suzong's empress.

sentences.zh: 母和政公主。

translations.literal: His mother was Princess Hezheng.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Princess Hezheng.

sentences.zh: 父潭，官至太僕卿、駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: His father Tan rose to Grand Master of the Stud and Commandant Escort of the Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tan rose to Grand Master of the Stud and Commandant Escort of the Son-in-Law.

sentences.zh: 晟少無檢操，代宗於諸甥之中，特加撫鞠，俾與太子、諸王同學，授詩書，恩寵罕比。

translations.literal: Sheng in youth lacked restraint in conduct; among all his nephews Daizong singled him out for special nurturing, had him study together with the crown prince and the princes, and taught him the classics; his favor was rarely matched.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng in youth lacked restraint in conduct. Among all his nephews Daizong singled him out for special nurturing, had him study together with the crown prince and the princes, and taught him the classics. His favor was rarely matched.

sentences.zh: 累試太常卿。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly tried in the post of Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly appointed Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 德宗即位，以與晟幼同硯席，尤親之。

translations.literal: When Dezong acceded, because he had shared desk and mat with Sheng in youth, he was especially close to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong acceded, because he had shared desk and mat with Sheng in youth, he was especially close to him.

sentences.zh: 涇師之亂，從幸奉天，晟密啟曰：「願受詔入京城，遊說群賊，冀其攜貳。

translations.literal: During the Jingshi mutiny, following the emperor's flight to Fengtian, Sheng secretly memorialized, saying, "I wish to receive an edict to enter the capital, persuade the rebel bands, and hope to make them waver and divide.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingshi mutiny, following the emperor's flight to Fengtian, Sheng secretly memorialized, saying, "I wish to receive an edict to enter the capital, persuade the rebel bands, and hope to make them waver and divide.

sentences.zh: 」德宗壯而許之。

translations.literal: " Dezong admired this and granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong admired this and granted his request.

sentences.zh: 晟與賊帥多有舊，出入其門說誘之。

translations.literal: Sheng had old ties with many of the rebel chiefs and went in and out of their gates to persuade and entice them.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng had old ties with many of the rebel chiefs and went in and out of their gates to persuade and entice them.

sentences.zh: 事泄，為硃泚所擒，械之於獄。

translations.literal: When the affair was exposed, he was seized by Zhu Ci and fettered in prison.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was exposed, he was seized by Zhu Ci and fettered in prison.

sentences.zh: 晟有力，乃於獄中穿垣破械而遁，落發為僧，間道歸行在。

translations.literal: Sheng was strong; he then tunneled through the prison wall, broke his fetters, and escaped, shaved his head and became a monk, and by hidden paths returned to the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was strong. He tunneled through the prison wall, broke his fetters, and escaped. He shaved his head and became a monk, then by hidden paths returned to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 遷將作少監。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Imperial Construction.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Imperial Construction.

sentences.zh: 元和初，檢校工部尚書、興元尹、山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: At the start of Yuanhe he was made Acting Minister of Works, Governor of Xingyuan, and Military Commissioner of Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yuanhe he was made Acting Minister of Works, Governor of Xingyuan, and Military Commissioner of Shannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 罷鎮入朝，以違詔進奉，為御史元稹所劾，詔宥之。

translations.literal: When he left his post and entered court, because he had presented tribute in violation of an edict, he was impeached by the censor Yuan Zhen; an edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: When he left his post and entered court, he was impeached by the censor Yuan Zhen for presenting tribute in violation of an edict. An edict pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 俄充入回鶻冊立使，復命，遷左金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he served as envoy to the Uighurs to invest their ruler; upon his return he was promoted to Grand General of the Left Jinwu Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he served as envoy to the Uighurs to invest their ruler. Upon his return he was promoted to Grand General of the Left Jinwu Guard.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子少保。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously appointed Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: =王子顏=

translations.literal: = Wang Ziyan =
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ziyan

sentences.zh: 王子顏，瑯邪臨沂人，莊憲皇后之父也。

translations.literal: Wang Ziyan, a native of Linyi in Langye, was the father of Empress Zhuangxian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ziyan, a native of Linyi in Langye, was the father of Empress Zhuangxian.

sentences.zh: 祖思敬，少從軍，累試太子賓客。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sijing entered the army in youth and was repeatedly appointed Counselor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sijing entered the army in youth and was repeatedly appointed Counselor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 父難得，有勇決，善騎射，天寶初為河源軍使。

translations.literal: His father Nan'de was brave and resolute, skilled in horsemanship and archery, and at the start of Tianbao was commissioner of the Heyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Nan'de was brave and resolute and skilled in horsemanship and archery. At the start of Tianbao he was commissioner of the Heyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃贊普王子郎支都有勇，乘諳真馬，寶鈿裝鞍，出陣求鬥，無敢與校者。

translations.literal: Langzhidu, a son of the Tibetan tsenpo, was brave; riding the horse Anzhen with a saddle adorned in jeweled inlay, he came out to the battle line seeking combat, and none dared to match him.
translations.idiomatic: Langzhidu, a son of the Tibetan tsenpo, was brave. Riding the horse Anzhen with a jeweled saddle, he came out to the battle line seeking combat, and none dared to match him.

sentences.zh: 難得挾槍奮馬突前，刺殺郎支都，斬其首，傳於京師。

translations.literal: Nan'de grasped his lance, spurred his horse forward in a rush, stabbed and killed Langzhidu, cut off his head, and sent it to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Nan'de grasped his lance, spurred his horse forward in a rush, stabbed and killed Langzhidu, cut off his head, and sent it to the capital.

sentences.zh: 軍還，玄宗召見之，令於殿前乘馬挾槍作刺郎支都之狀。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Xuanzong summoned him and ordered him to ride a horse before the hall, lance in hand, and act out the thrust that killed Langzhidu.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, Xuanzong summoned him and ordered him to ride before the hall, lance in hand, and act out the thrust that killed Langzhidu.

sentences.zh: 賜以錦袍金帶，累拜金吾將軍同正員。

translations.literal: He was granted a brocade robe and gold belt and was successively appointed Regular Assistant General of the Jinwu Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a brocade robe and gold belt and was successively appointed Regular Assistant General of the Jinwu Guard.

sentences.zh: ，從哥舒翰擊吐蕃於積石，虜吐谷渾王子悉弄參及子婿悉頰藏而還，累拜左武衛將軍、關西遊奕使。

translations.literal: , he followed Geshu Han to attack the Tibetans at Jishi, captured the Tuyuhun prince Sinong Can and his son-in-law Sinuocang, and returned; he was successively appointed General of the Left Martial Guard and Commissioner of the Guanxi Mobile Corps.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Geshu Han to attack the Tibetans at Jishi, captured the Tuyuhun prince Sinong Can and his son-in-law Sinuocang, and returned. He was successively appointed General of the Left Martial Guard and Commissioner of the Guanxi Mobile Corps.

sentences.zh: 九載，擊吐蕃，收五橋，拔樹敦城，補白水軍使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he attacked the Tibetans, recovered Wuqiao, captured Shudun city, and was appointed commissioner of the Baishui Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he attacked the Tibetans, recovered Wuqiao, captured Shudun city, and was appointed commissioner of the Baishui Army.

sentences.zh: 十三載，從收九曲，加特進。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he followed in the recovery of the Nine Bends and was granted the special advancement.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he followed in the recovery of the Nine Bends and was granted the special advancement.

sentences.zh: 祿山之叛，從哥舒翰戰於潼關；

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled, he followed Geshu Han to fight at Tong Pass;
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan rebelled, he followed Geshu Han to fight at Tong Pass;

sentences.zh: 關門不守，從肅宗幸靈武。

translations.literal: when the pass was not held, he followed Suzong in the flight to Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: when the pass was not held, he followed Suzong in the flight to Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 時行在闕軍賞，難得進絹三千疋及金銀器等。

translations.literal: At the time the imperial camp lacked funds for military rewards; Nan'de presented three thousand bolts of silk and gold and silver vessels.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the imperial camp lacked funds for military rewards. Nan'de presented three thousand bolts of silk and gold and silver vessels.

sentences.zh: 至德初，試衛尉卿、興平軍使，兼鳳翔都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: At the start of Zhide he was tried as Minister of the Guard, commissioner of the Xingping Army, and concurrently Commander of Military Affairs at Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Zhide he was appointed Minister of the Guard, commissioner of the Xingping Army, and concurrently Commander of Military Affairs at Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 進收京城，與賊軍戰。

translations.literal: Advancing to recover the capital, he fought the rebel army.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to recover the capital, he fought the rebel army.

sentences.zh: 其下靳元曜戰酣墮馬，難得馳救之，賊射之中眉，皮穿披下鄣目。

translations.literal: His subordinate Jin Yuanyao, in the heat of battle, fell from his horse; Nan'de galloped to rescue him, and the rebels shot him in the brow; the skin was pierced and hung down over the cheek guard before his eyes.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinate Jin Yuanyao, in the heat of battle, fell from his horse. Nan'de galloped to rescue him, and the rebels shot him in the brow. The skin was pierced and hung down over the cheek guard before his eyes.

sentences.zh: 難得自拔去箭，並皮掣洛，馳馬復戰，血流被面，而抗賊不已。

translations.literal: Nan'de himself pulled out the arrow, tore away the hanging skin, spurred his horse and fought again; blood covered his face, yet he resisted the rebels without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Nan'de himself pulled out the arrow, tore away the hanging skin, spurred his horse and fought again. Blood covered his face, yet he resisted the rebels without cease.

sentences.zh: 肅宗深嘉之。

translations.literal: Suzong deeply commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong deeply commended him.

sentences.zh: 從郭子儀攻安慶緒於相州，累封瑯邪郡公，英武軍使。

translations.literal: He followed Guo Ziyi in attacking An Qingxu at Xiangzhou and was successively enfeoffed Duke of Langye commandery and made commissioner of the Yingwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Guo Ziyi in attacking An Qingxu at Xiangzhou and was successively enfeoffed Duke of Langye and made commissioner of the Yingwu Army.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈潞州大都督。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously appointed Governor-General of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed Governor-General of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 子顏少從父征役，累官金紫光祿大夫、檢校衛尉卿，生后而卒。

translations.literal: Ziyan from youth followed his father on campaigns, rose to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and Acting Minister of the Guard, and died after the empress was born.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyan from youth followed his father on campaigns, rose to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and Acting Minister of the Guard, and died after the empress was born.

sentences.zh: 順宗內禪，以后生憲宗皇帝，褒贈先代：思敬司徒，難得太傅，子顏太師。

translations.literal: When Shunzong abdicated internally and the empress had borne Emperor Xianzong, earlier generations were honored posthumously: Sijing was made Minister over the Masses, Nan'de Grand Tutor, and Ziyan Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzong abdicated internally and the empress had borne Emperor Xianzong, earlier generations were honored posthumously: Sijing was made Minister over the Masses, Nan'de Grand Tutor, and Ziyan Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 顏子重榮，官至福王傅；

translations.literal: Ziyan's son Zhongrong rose to Tutor to the Prince of Fu;
translations.idiomatic: Ziyan's son Zhongrong rose to Tutor to the Prince of Fu;

sentences.zh: 用，官至太子賓客、金吾將軍。

translations.literal: Yong rose to Counselor to the Heir Apparent and General of the Jinwu Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yong rose to Counselor to the Heir Apparent and General of the Jinwu Guard.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：戚里之賢，避寵畏權。

translations.literal: Comment: Among the virtuous of the imperial kin, they shunned favor and feared power.
translations.idiomatic: Comment: Among the virtuous of the imperial kin, they shunned favor and feared power.

sentences.zh: 不恤禍患，鮮能保全。

translations.literal: Those who did not spare themselves from calamity — few could preserve themselves intact.
translations.idiomatic: Those who did not spare themselves from calamity — few could preserve themselves intact.

sentences.zh: 福盈者敗，勢壓者顛。

translations.literal: Those whose fortune is full are ruined; those whose power overbears are overturned.
translations.idiomatic: Those whose fortune runs full are ruined; those whose power presses too hard are overturned.

sentences.zh: 武之惟良，明於自然。

translations.literal: Among the Wu, Weiliang alone was clear about the natural order.
translations.idiomatic: Of the Wu clan, Weiliang alone understood how nature works.
